modules.title: Light cones in time and space
modules.doc:
Causal future and past of sets in time and space and in Minkowski spacetime.

## i. Overview

Causal future and past of sets in time and space and in Minkowski spacetime. Causal futures of
compact sets are closed and causal diamonds are compact.

## ii. Key results

- `causalFuture` : The causal future of a set of spacetime points, in units where the speed of light
  is `1`.
- `causalPast` : The causal past of a set of spacetime points.
- `precedes_iff_time_space` : In any speed-of-light units the existing geometric causal relation has
  the familiar elapsed-time and spatial-distance characterization.
- `causallyFollows_iff_norm` : The existing Lorentzian causal order is equivalently the spatial norm
  bounded by elapsed Lorentz time.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Minkowski causal geometry for Green operators
- B. Causal support of the retarded solution

## iv. References

None.

## A. Minkowski causal geometry for Green operators

Lemmas: `causallyFollows_iff_displacement`, `causallyFollows_iff_norm`, `norm_space_eq_spatialPart`,
`precedes_iff_time_space`, `isClosed_causalFuture_zero`, `causalFuture_eq_add`,
`isClosed_causalFuture`, `causalPast_eq_add_neg`, `isClosed_causalPast`,
`component_bound_of_causalDiamond` and more.

## B. Causal support of the retarded solution

- `causalFuture` : The causal future of a set of spacetime points, in units where the speed of light
  is `1`.
- `causalPast` : The causal past of a set of spacetime points.

Lemmas: `isClosed_causalFuture`.

declarations.name: Minkowski.causallyFollows_iff_displacement
declarations.doc: Causal precedence depends only on the displacement between events.
declarations.statement:
lemma causallyFollows_iff_displacement (p q : SpaceTime d) :
    causallyFollows p q ↔ causallyFollows 0 (q - p)

declarations.name: Minkowski.causallyFollows_iff_norm
declarations.doc:
The existing Lorentzian causal order is equivalently the spatial norm bounded by elapsed
Lorentz time. Nonnegative elapsed time follows from this inequality.
declarations.statement:
lemma causallyFollows_iff_norm (p q : SpaceTime d) :
    causallyFollows p q ↔ ‖(q - p).spatialPart‖ ≤ (q - p).timeComponent

declarations.doc: Minkowski causal geometry reuses the existing Lorentzian future relation.
declarations.statement: def causalRelation (d : ℕ) : CausalRelation (SpaceTime d)

declarations.name: Minkowski.norm_space_eq_spatialPart
declarations.doc: Physlib's physical-space norm agrees with the Euclidean norm of the Lorentz spatial part.
declarations.statement: lemma norm_space_eq_spatialPart (p : SpaceTime d) : ‖p.space‖ = ‖p.spatialPart‖

declarations.name: Minkowski.precedes_iff_time_space
declarations.doc:
In any speed-of-light units the existing geometric causal relation has the familiar
elapsed-time and spatial-distance characterization. This is an application representation.
declarations.statement:
lemma precedes_iff_time_space (c : SpeedOfLight) (p q : SpaceTime d) :
    (causalRelation d).Precedes p q ↔
      (p.time c).val ≤ (q.time c).val ∧
        ‖q.space - p.space‖ ≤ (c : ℝ) * ((q.time c).val - (p.time c).val)

declarations.doc: Futures are translations of the existing future cone, combined over the source set.
declarations.statement:

declarations.doc: Causal futures of compact source sets are closed.

declarations.doc: Causal pasts are translations of the negated future cone.
declarations.statement:

    (causalRelation d).causalPast K = K + -((causalRelation d).causalFuture {0})

declarations.name: Minkowski.component_bound_of_causalDiamond
declarations.doc: Every component in a causal diamond is bounded by the bounds on its endpoint sets.
declarations.statement:
lemma component_bound_of_causalDiamond {A B : ℝ} (hA : 0 ≤ A) (hB : 0 ≤ B)
    {k x l : SpaceTime d} (hk : ‖k‖ ≤ A) (hl : ‖l‖ ≤ B)
    (hkx : (causalRelation d).Precedes k x) (hxl : (causalRelation d).Precedes x l)

modules.title: The gamma matrices need four dimensions
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A Clifford family is a choice of `n × n` complex matrices `γ^μ`, one for each Lorentz index,
with `γ^μ γ^ν + γ^ν γ^μ = 2 η^{μν} 1`. Dirac (1928) found one with `n = 4`, and no smaller
size works. Each `γ^μ` squares to `± 1`, so it is invertible, and `γ^0 γ^1 = -γ^1 γ^0` forces
`det (γ^0 γ^1) = (-1)ⁿ det (γ^0 γ^1)`: the size is even. Size two is excluded by the three
Pauli matrices: `γ^0, i γ^1, i γ^2, i γ^3` would be four anticommuting `2 × 2` involutions, and
`2 × 2` holds at most three. The Dirac endomorphisms `gamma` of Physlib, written as `4 × 4`
matrices, attain the bound.

## ii. Key results

- `IsCliffordFamily` : the relation `γ^μ γ^ν + γ^ν γ^μ = 2 η^{μν} 1`.
- `IsCliffordFamily.even` : a Clifford family has even size.
- `IsCliffordFamily.ne_two` : there are no `2 × 2` Clifford families.
- `IsCliffordFamily.four_le` : a nonempty Clifford family has size at least four.
- `isCliffordFamily_gamma` : the Dirac gamma matrices are a Clifford family.
- `isLeast_size_isCliffordFamily` : the smallest size of a Clifford family is four.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Clifford families
- B. The size is even
- C. Size two is excluded
- D. Dirac's matrices attain the bound

## iv. References

* P. A. M. Dirac, *The quantum theory of the electron*, Proc. R. Soc. London A 117 (1928)
  610–624.

    IsLeast {n : ℕ | n ≠ 0 ∧ ∃ γ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ,
      IsCliffordFamily γ} 4

modules.title: The boost weights of a Weyl spinor
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

Along the `z`-axis the `SL(2,ℂ)` boost is the diagonal matrix `diag (t, t⁻¹)`, so both
Weyl bases are bases of boost eigenvectors: the first component carries weight `+1` and
the second weight `-1`.  A Weyl spinor is a half-vector.

## ii. Key results

- `weylWeight` : the boost weight of a Weyl-spinor index
- `rightHandedWeyl_rep_boostAxis_two_basis` : the right-handed Weyl basis diagonalises the
  `z`-boost, with weights `±1`
- `leftHandedWeyl_rep_boostAxis_two_basis` : the left-handed Weyl basis diagonalises the `z`-boost,
  with weights `±1`

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The boost weight along the `z`-axis

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: The Weyl metric as an element of `SL(2, ℂ)`
modules.doc:
The symplectic form `ε` as a group element, and the identities moving it past a group element.

## i. Overview

The Weyl metric `Fermion.metricRaw = !![0, 1; -1, 0]` has determinant one, so it is itself an
element of `SL(2, ℂ)`, written `Lorentz.SL2C.epsilon`. In that form it is the invariant symplectic
form, `gᵀ ε g = ε`. Contracting spinor indices needs the single-index version of that invariance: a
factor of `(g⁻¹)ᵀ`, or of `(g⁻¹)ᴴ`, moved across `ε` becomes a factor of `g`, or of its entrywise
conjugate, on the other slot. Those are `metricRaw_comm` and `metricRaw_comm_star` at `g⁻¹`, read
entrywise. Alongside this, `LeftHandedWeyl.metricVal_rep` states the invariance of `εᵃᵃ` as the
plain equation on the tensor product, rather than through the intertwining property of
`LeftHandedWeyl.metric`.

## ii. Key results

- `Fermion.LeftHandedWeyl.metricVal_rep` : `εᵃᵃ` is invariant under `SL(2, ℂ)`.
- `Lorentz.SL2C.epsilon` : the Weyl metric as an element of `SL(2, ℂ)`.
- `Lorentz.SL2C.transpose_mul_epsilon_mul` : `ε` is the invariant symplectic form.
- `Lorentz.SL2C.sum_epsilon_mul_inv_transpose`,
  `Lorentz.SL2C.sum_epsilon_mul_inv_conjTranspose` : the single-index forms.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Invariance of the left metric
- B. The symplectic form as an element of `SL(2, ℂ)`

## iv. References

The Weyl metrics and `Fermion.metricRaw` are in `Physlib.Relativity.Fermions.Weyl.Metric`.

## B. The symplectic form as an element of `SL(2, ℂ)`

`ε = metricRaw` has determinant one, so it lies in `SL(2,ℂ)`, and `gᵀ ε g = ε` for every `g`
there. The single-index identities move a factor of `(g⁻¹)ᵀ` or `(g⁻¹)ᴴ` across `ε`, where it
becomes a factor of `g` or of its conjugate on the other slot: they are `metricRaw_comm` and
`metricRaw_comm_star` at `g⁻¹`, read entrywise.

      = ∑ b : Fin 2, star (g.1 b l) * epsilon.1 b a

modules.title: Schwarzschild's incompressible fluid sphere and its junction with the exterior solution
modules.doc:
Junction of Schwarzschild's incompressible fluid sphere with the exterior Schwarzschild metric.

## i. Overview

In his second 1916 paper, Schwarzschild solved Einstein's equations for a static sphere of
incompressible fluid of constant density `ρ₀`. The interior space is a portion of a
three-sphere of curvature radius `Rc`, with `Rc ^ 2 = 3 / (κ ρ₀)` (`κ = 8 π G`, `c = 1`),
and the surface of the fluid sits at the polar angle `χ_a` with `sin χ_a = Ra / Rc`, where
`Ra` is the areal radius of the surface. In the areal radius `r = Rc sin χ` the interior metric
coefficients are

- `g_tt = ((3 cos χ_a - cos χ) / 2) ^ 2 = (3 / 2 cos χ_a - 1 / 2 √(1 - r ^ 2 / Rc ^ 2)) ^ 2`,
- `g_rr = 1 / (1 - r ^ 2 / Rc ^ 2)`,

while outside the sphere the metric is the exterior Schwarzschild solution with
`g_tt = 1 - α / r`, `g_rr = 1 / (1 - α / r)` and `α = Ra ^ 3 / Rc ^ 2`. The pressure is
`ρ₀ + p = ρ₀ 2 cos χ_a / (3 cos χ_a - cos χ)`.

This file takes the two metrics and the pressure as given (the field equations are not
verified here) and proves the elementary properties of the junction at `r = Ra`: continuity
of `g_tt` and `g_rr`, differentiability of the glued `g_tt`, non-differentiability of the glued
`g_rr` in the curvature coordinate `r`, the vanishing of the pressure at the surface, and the
Schwarzschild bound `cos χ_a > 1 / 3` (equivalently `Ra > 9 / 8 α`) for the central pressure to
be positive.

## ii. Key results

- `IncompressibleSphere` contains the input data: `Rc`, `Ra`, `ρ₀` with `0 < Ra < Rc` and
  `0 < ρ₀`.
- `rs_div_Ra`: Schwarzschild's relation (40), `α / Ra = sin χ_a ^ 2`.
- `pressure_chia`: the pressure vanishes at the surface.
- `pressure_zero_pos_iff`: the central pressure is positive if and only if `cos χ_a > 1 / 3`.
- `one_third_lt_cosChia_iff_rs`: `cos χ_a > 1 / 3` if and only if `9 / 8 α < Ra`.
- `gttIn_Ra`, `grrIn_Ra`: the interior and exterior formulas agree at `r = Ra`.
- `gttGlue_hasDerivAt`: the glued `g_tt` is differentiable at `Ra` with derivative `Ra / Rc ^ 2`.
- `grrGlue_not_differentiableAt`: the glued `g_rr` is continuous but not differentiable at
  `Ra` (one-sided derivatives `2 Ra / (Rc ^ 2 cos χ_a ^ 4)` and `- Ra / (Rc ^ 2 cos χ_a ^ 4)`).

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The input data
- B. The Schwarzschild radius and the angle of the surface
- C. The pressure
  - C.1. Pressure at the surface and at the centre
  - C.2. The bound `cos χ_a > 1 / 3`
- D. The metric coefficients
  - D.1. The interior metric in the angle `χ`
  - D.2. The values at the surface agree
- E. Derivatives of the metric coefficients at the surface
  - E.1. Two auxiliary derivatives
  - E.2. Derivatives of `g_tt`
  - E.3. Derivatives of `g_rr`
- F. The glued metric coefficients
- G. Consequences for the junction
- H. A numerical instance

## iv. References

- K. Schwarzschild, "Uber das Gravitationsfeld einer Kugel aus inkompressibler Flussigkeit nach
  der Einsteinschen Theorie", Sitzungsberichte der Koniglich Preussischen Akademie der
  Wissenschaften (1916), 424-434. English translation by S. Antoci, arXiv:physics/9912033.
  Equations (28), (29), (30), (35), (36), (39), (40) and the discussion on pages 8-9 of the
  translation (pressure diverging at `cos χ_a = 1 / 3`, limit `9 / 8 α`).
- A. Lichnerowicz, "Theories relativistes de la gravitation et de l'electromagnetisme",
  Masson (1955), chapter III, sections 27-29 (junction conditions).

## F. The glued metric coefficients

The glued coefficients use the interior formula for `r ≤ Ra` and the exterior formula
beyond. The glued `g_tt` is differentiable at `Ra`; the glued `g_rr` is continuous but not
differentiable at `Ra`, since its one-sided derivatives differ.

## G. Consequences for the junction

In a Gaussian coordinate `l` along the radius, `dr / dl = 1 / √g_rr` and
`d g_tt / dl = g_tt' / √g_rr`. Both quantities take the same value at `Ra` from the two
formulas (Lichnerowicz, chapter III, section 28, evaluated at the surface). The coordinate `l`
itself is not constructed here.

## H. A numerical instance

The sphere with `Rc = 1`, `Ra = 3 / 5` and `ρ₀ = 1`: `cos χ_a = 4 / 5`, `α = 27 / 125`,
`9 / 8 α < Ra`, central pressure `1 / 7`.

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere
declarations.doc:
Schwarzschild's incompressible fluid sphere: the curvature radius `Rc` of the interior
spherical space (`Rc ^ 2 = 3 / (κ ρ₀)`, Schwarzschild (37)), the areal radius `Ra` of the
surface (Schwarzschild's `P_o`, (39)) and the constant density `ρ₀`, with `0 < Ra < Rc` and
`0 < ρ₀`.
declarations.statement:
structure IncompressibleSphere where
  /-- The curvature radius of the interior spherical space. -/
  Rc : ℝ
  /-- The areal radius of the surface of the fluid. -/

  /-- The radius of the surface is positive. -/

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.rs
declarations.doc:
The Schwarzschild radius `α = (κ ρ₀ / 3) P_o ^ 3 = Ra ^ 3 / Rc ^ 2` of the sphere,
Schwarzschild (40).
declarations.statement: def rs : ℝ

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.chia
declarations.doc: The polar angle `χ_a` of the surface, `sin χ_a = Ra / Rc`, Schwarzschild (28).
declarations.statement: def chia : ℝ

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.cosChia
declarations.doc: The cosine of the angle of the surface, written as `√(1 - Ra ^ 2 / Rc ^ 2)`.
declarations.statement: def cosChia : ℝ

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.one_sub_sq_div_sq_pos
declarations.statement: lemma one_sub_sq_div_sq_pos : 0 < 1 - S.Ra ^ 2 / S.Rc ^ 2

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.cosChia_sq
declarations.statement: lemma cosChia_sq : S.cosChia ^ 2 = 1 - S.Ra ^ 2 / S.Rc ^ 2

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.cosChia_eq_cos_chia
declarations.doc: `cosChia` is the cosine of `chia`.
declarations.statement: lemma cosChia_eq_cos_chia : S.cosChia = Real.cos S.chia

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.cosChia_pos
declarations.statement: lemma cosChia_pos : 0 < S.cosChia

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.cosChia_lt_one
declarations.statement: lemma cosChia_lt_one : S.cosChia < 1

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.rs_div_Ra
declarations.doc: Schwarzschild (40): `α / P_o = sin χ_a ^ 2`.
declarations.statement: lemma rs_div_Ra : S.rs / S.Ra = Real.sin S.chia ^ 2

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.rs_lt_Ra
declarations.doc: The surface of the sphere lies outside its Schwarzschild radius.
declarations.statement: lemma rs_lt_Ra : S.rs < S.Ra

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.pressure
declarations.doc:
The pressure of the fluid at the polar angle `χ`, Schwarzschild (30):
`ρ₀ + p = ρ₀ 2 cos χ_a / (3 cos χ_a - cos χ)`.
declarations.statement: def pressure (χ : ℝ) : ℝ

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.pressure_chia
declarations.doc: The pressure vanishes at the surface of the fluid.
declarations.statement: lemma pressure_chia : S.pressure S.chia = 0

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.pressure_zero
declarations.doc: The pressure at the centre, away from the critical value `cos χ_a = 1 / 3`.
declarations.statement:
lemma pressure_zero (h : 3 * S.cosChia ≠ 1) :
    S.pressure 0 = S.ρ₀ * (1 - S.cosChia) / (3 * S.cosChia - 1)

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.pressure_zero_pos
declarations.statement: lemma pressure_zero_pos (hsub : 1 / 3 < S.cosChia) : 0 < S.pressure 0

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.pressure_zero_pos_iff
declarations.doc:
The central pressure is positive if and only if `cos χ_a > 1 / 3`. For `cos χ_a < 1 / 3`
the formula (30) is negative at the centre; at `cos χ_a = 1 / 3` the division by zero of
Lean gives `pressure 0 = - ρ₀`. The divergence of the pressure at the critical value is not
a statement of this file.
declarations.statement: lemma pressure_zero_pos_iff : 0 < S.pressure 0 ↔ 1 / 3 < S.cosChia

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.one_third_lt_cosChia_iff_sq
declarations.statement: lemma one_third_lt_cosChia_iff_sq : 1 / 3 < S.cosChia ↔ S.Ra ^ 2 < 8 / 9 * S.Rc ^ 2

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.one_third_lt_cosChia_iff_Ra_lt
declarations.doc: `cos χ_a > 1 / 3` if and only if `Ra < √(8 / 9) Rc`.
declarations.statement: lemma one_third_lt_cosChia_iff_Ra_lt : 1 / 3 < S.cosChia ↔ S.Ra < √(8 / 9) * S.Rc

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.one_third_lt_cosChia_iff_rs
declarations.doc: `cos χ_a > 1 / 3` if and only if `9 / 8 α < Ra` (Schwarzschild, page 9).
declarations.statement: lemma one_third_lt_cosChia_iff_rs : 1 / 3 < S.cosChia ↔ 9 / 8 * S.rs < S.Ra

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.Ra_div_Rc_of_cosChia_eq
declarations.doc:
At the critical value `cos χ_a = 1 / 3` the ratio `Ra / Rc = sin χ_a` (Schwarzschild's
fall velocity, (42)) equals `√(8 / 9)`.
declarations.statement: lemma Ra_div_Rc_of_cosChia_eq (hc : S.cosChia = 1 / 3) : S.Ra / S.Rc = √(8 / 9)

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.gttIn
declarations.doc:
The interior coefficient `g_tt` in the areal radius `r`, Schwarzschild (35):
`(3 / 2 cos χ_a - 1 / 2 √(1 - r ^ 2 / Rc ^ 2)) ^ 2`.
declarations.statement: def gttIn (r : ℝ) : ℝ

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.grrIn
declarations.doc:
The interior coefficient `g_rr` in the areal radius `r`, Schwarzschild (35):
`1 / (1 - r ^ 2 / Rc ^ 2)`.
declarations.statement: def grrIn (r : ℝ) : ℝ

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.gttOut

declarations.statement: def gttOut (r : ℝ) : ℝ

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.grrOut
declarations.doc: The exterior coefficient `g_rr = 1 / (1 - α / r)`, Schwarzschild (36).
declarations.statement: def grrOut (r : ℝ) : ℝ

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.one_sub_sin_sq
declarations.statement:
lemma one_sub_sin_sq (χ : ℝ) :
    1 - (S.Rc * Real.sin χ) ^ 2 / S.Rc ^ 2 = Real.cos χ ^ 2

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.gttIn_Rc_mul_sin
declarations.doc: Schwarzschild (35): in the angle `χ`, `g_tt = ((3 cos χ_a - cos χ) / 2) ^ 2`.

    S.gttIn (S.Rc * Real.sin χ) = ((3 * S.cosChia - Real.cos χ) / 2) ^ 2

declarations.doc: Schwarzschild (35): in the angle `χ`, the coefficient of `dχ ^ 2` is `Rc ^ 2`.
declarations.statement:

    S.grrIn (S.Rc * Real.sin χ) * (S.Rc * Real.cos χ) ^ 2 = S.Rc ^ 2

declarations.statement: lemma gttIn_zero_of_cosChia_eq (hcrit : S.cosChia = 1 / 3) : S.gttIn 0 = 0

modules.title: Class IsLorentzDeriv
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A family of operators indexed by the four spacetime directions is a Lorentz derivative
when the representation of `SL(2,ℂ)` intertwines it through the columns of the Lorentz
matrix, as the jet derivatives on a jet algebra do. The iterated operator along a multiset
of directions then transforms by one column of the Lorentz matrix per slot
(`rep_iteratedD_ofFn`), which is the law `IsLorentzDerivTransforms` and its covariant form
`IsLorentzCovDerivTransforms` record for a family of derivative symbols.

## ii. Key results

- `IsLorentzDerivTransforms` : a family of derivative symbols `F : s ↦ [∂_s ψ^φ]`, indexed by the
  dual of a value space `V` carrying a representation of `SL(2,ℂ)`, transforms as the derivative
  symbols of a Lorentz-covariant field: each ordered symbol mixes into all tuples of directions by
  the per-slot columns of the Lorentz matrix, while the value index transforms by the contragredient
  action `rep.dual` on the dual of `V`
- `IsLorentzCovDerivTransforms` : a family of *covariant*-derivative symbols, indexed by ordered
  tuples of directions (covariant derivatives do not commute) and by the dual of a Lorentz
  representation `V`, transforms as the covariant derivatives of a Lorentz-covariant field: each
  derivative slot mixes by the columns of the Lorentz matrix, while the value index transforms by
  the contragredient action `rep.dual` on the dual of `V` — the ordered-tuple analogue of
  `IsLorentzDerivTransforms`
- `rep_iteratedD_ofFn` : the Lorentz transformation of iterated derivatives: for a Lorentz
  derivative the ordered derivative symbol `D_{l 0} ⋯ D_{l (n-1)} x` mixes into all tuples of
  directions, with one Lorentz matrix factor per slot

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Lorentz-covariant families of derivative symbols

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: Representation.trivial_dual_apply
declarations.doc: The dual of the trivial representation acts trivially.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.Representation.trivial_dual_apply {k G V : Type*} [CommSemiring k]
    [Group G] [AddCommMonoid V] [Module k V] (g : G) (φ : Module.Dual k V) :
    (Representation.trivial k G V).dual g φ = φ

declarations.name: Lorentz.iteratedD
declarations.doc:
The iterated operator `D_s = D_{ν₁} ⋯ D_{νₙ}` of a pairwise-commuting family of
endomorphisms along a multiset `s` of indices. Commutativity is what makes the
operator well-defined on a multiset, i.e. independent of any ordering of `s`.
declarations.statement:
def iteratedD {ι : Type*} (D : ι → A →ₗ[ℂ] A)
    (hD : ∀ i j, (D i).comp (D j) = (D j).comp (D i)) (s : Multiset ι) : A →ₗ[ℂ] A

declarations.name: Lorentz.iteratedD_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedD_zero {ι : Type*} (D : ι → A →ₗ[ℂ] A)
    (hD : ∀ i j, (D i).comp (D j) = (D j).comp (D i)) :
    iteratedD D hD (0 : Multiset ι) = LinearMap.id

declarations.name: Lorentz.iteratedD_cons
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedD_cons {ι : Type*} (D : ι → A →ₗ[ℂ] A)
    (hD : ∀ i j, (D i).comp (D j) = (D j).comp (D i)) (κ : ι) (s : Multiset ι) :
    iteratedD D hD (κ ::ₘ s) = (D κ).comp (iteratedD D hD s)

declarations.name: Lorentz.iteratedD_singleton
declarations.doc: The iterated operator of a singleton is the operator itself.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedD_singleton {ι : Type*} (D : ι → A →ₗ[ℂ] A)
    (hD : ∀ i j, (D i).comp (D j) = (D j).comp (D i)) (κ : ι) :
    iteratedD D hD {κ} = D κ

declarations.name: Lorentz.iteratedD_add
declarations.doc:
The iterated operator is additive in the multiset of directions: applying along
`s + t` is applying along `t` and then along `s`.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedD_add {ι : Type*} (D : ι → A →ₗ[ℂ] A)
    (hD : ∀ i j, (D i).comp (D j) = (D j).comp (D i)) (s t : Multiset ι) :
    iteratedD D hD (s + t) = (iteratedD D hD s).comp (iteratedD D hD t)

declarations.name: Lorentz.iteratedD_cons'
declarations.doc:
The companion of `iteratedD_cons`, peeling the new operator on the inside: for a
commuting family the extra operator may equally be applied first.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedD_cons' {ι : Type*} (D : ι → A →ₗ[ℂ] A)
    (hD : ∀ i j, (D i).comp (D j) = (D j).comp (D i)) (κ : ι) (s : Multiset ι) :
    iteratedD D hD (κ ::ₘ s) = (iteratedD D hD s).comp (D κ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.iteratedD_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedD_mul (D : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → A →ₗ[ℂ] A)
    (D_comm : ∀ μ ν, (D μ).comp (D ν) = (D ν).comp (D μ))
    (D_mul : ∀ (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (b₁ b₂ : A),
      D μ (b₁ * b₂) = D μ b₁ * b₂ + b₁ * D μ b₂)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (b₁ b₂ : A) :
    Lorentz.iteratedD D D_comm s (b₁ * b₂) =
      (s.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        Lorentz.iteratedD D D_comm p.1 b₁ * Lorentz.iteratedD D D_comm p.2 b₂).sum

declarations.name: Lorentz.IsLorentzDeriv
declarations.doc:
A family of operators indexed by the spacetime directions is a **Lorentz derivative**
when the representation of `SL(2,ℂ)` intertwines it through the columns of the Lorentz
matrix. The class needs only the module structure, so it applies uniformly to any
representation space.
declarations.statement:
class IsLorentzDeriv {M : Type} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module ℂ M]
    (rep : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) M) (D : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M →ₗ[ℂ] M) where
  rep_deriv {Λ μ x} : rep Λ (D μ x) =
    ∑ a, (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup Λ).1 a μ : ℝ) : ℂ) • D a (rep Λ x)

declarations.name: Lorentz.IsLorentzDerivTransforms
declarations.doc:
A family of derivative symbols `F : s ↦ [∂_s ψ^φ]`, indexed by the dual of a value
space `V` carrying a representation of `SL(2,ℂ)`, **transforms as the derivative
symbols of a Lorentz-covariant field**: each ordered symbol mixes into all tuples of
directions by the per-slot columns of the Lorentz matrix, while the value index
transforms by the contragredient action `rep.dual` on the dual of `V`. This is the
general form of the Lorentz law `GaugeAlgebraRealization.lorentz_apply`, for a field valued in an
arbitrary Lorentz representation — the trivial representation for scalars, the Weyl
representations for fermions, and their conjugates for the barred fields. At `n = 0`
it reduces to the homogeneous law `Λ • F₀^φ = F₀^{Λ^{-⊤} φ}`.
declarations.statement:
def IsLorentzDerivTransforms {k V : Type*} [CommRing k] [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V]
    [Module k A]
    (repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) A) (rep : Representation k SL(2,ℂ) V)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual k V →ₗ[k] A) : Prop

declarations.name: Lorentz.IsLorentzCovDerivTransforms
declarations.doc:
A family of *covariant*-derivative symbols, indexed by ordered tuples of
directions (covariant derivatives do not commute) and by the dual of a Lorentz
representation `V`, **transforms as the covariant derivatives of a
Lorentz-covariant field**: each derivative slot mixes by the columns of the Lorentz
matrix, while the value index transforms by the contragredient action `rep.dual` on
the dual of `V` — the ordered-tuple analogue of `IsLorentzDerivTransforms`.
declarations.statement:
def IsLorentzCovDerivTransforms {k V : Type*} [CommRing k] [AddCommGroup V]
    [Module k V] [Module k A] (repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) A)
    (rep : Representation k SL(2,ℂ) V)
    (F : {n : ℕ} → (Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) → Module.Dual k V →ₗ[k] A) : Prop

declarations.name: Lorentz.IsLorentzCovDerivTransforms.neg_one_apply
declarations.doc:
**At the centre the derivative slots do not mix.** The element `-1` of `SL(2,ℂ)` covers
the identity Lorentz transformation, so the sum over tuples collapses to the single term
`p = l` and only the value index moves.

declarations.name: Lorentz.IsLorentzDeriv.rep_iteratedD_ofFn
declarations.doc:
**The Lorentz transformation of iterated derivatives**: for a Lorentz derivative the
ordered derivative symbol `D_{l 0} ⋯ D_{l (n-1)} x` mixes into all tuples of
directions, with one Lorentz matrix factor per slot.
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_iteratedD_ofFn [IsLorentzDeriv rep D]
    (D_comm : ∀ μ ν, (D μ).comp (D ν) = (D ν).comp (D μ))
    (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (x : A) :
    rep Λ (iteratedD D D_comm (List.ofFn l) x) =
      ∑ p : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3),
        (∏ i, (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup Λ).1 (p i) (l i) : ℝ) : ℂ)) •
          iteratedD D D_comm (List.ofFn p) (rep Λ x)

modules.title: The light-cone basis of an axis
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A tuple of spacetime directions can be re-read in the light-cone basis along a boost axis:
`lightConeCoeff` gives the four light-cone directions `D₀ - Dᵢ`, `D₀ + Dᵢ` and the two
transverse ones, and `lightConeCoeffInv` the inverse change of basis.  The point of the
change of basis is `sum_boostAxis_lightConeCoeff`: the four directions are eigenvectors of
the boost along the axis, of weight `lightConeWeight` — `+2` for `D₀ - Dᵢ`, `-2` for
`D₀ + Dᵢ`, and `0` for the transverse directions.

On a tuple of slots the two coefficient matrices are still inverse to one another
(`sum_prod_lightConeCoeff`, `sum_prod_lightConeCoeffInv`) and the weights add
(`sum_prod_lightConeCoeff`).  That is what the classification of the Lorentz invariants in
`LorentzGroup/Invariants` runs on: it writes a coefficient tensor in this basis and keeps
only the piece of total weight zero.

## ii. Key results

- `lightConeCoeff` : the four light-cone directions along the `i`-th axis, written as coefficient
  vectors on the coordinate directions: `D₀ - Dᵢ`, `D₀ + Dᵢ`, and the two transverse directions
- `lightConeWeight` : the boost weight carried by each light-cone direction: `+2` for `D₀ - Dᵢ`,
  `-2` for `D₀ + Dᵢ`, and `0` for the two transverse directions
- `sum_boostAxis_lightConeCoeff` : the light-cone directions are eigenvectors of the boost
- `lightConeCoeffInv` : the coordinate directions written back in the light-cone basis: `D₀` and
  `Dᵢ` are the half-sum and half-difference of `D₀ ∓ Dᵢ`, and the transverse directions are
  themselves
- `sum_prod_lightConeCoeff` : the scalar behind `lightConeDeriv_mem`: the boost acts on a light-cone
  multi-index slot by slot, so the product of the per-slot eigenvalues factors out
- `sum_prod_lightConeCoeffInv` : the two coefficient matrices are inverse slot by slot, hence
  inverse on multi-indices; this is `sum_prod_lightConeCoeff` with the two factors the other way
  round

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The light-cone basis of an axis

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: Lorentz.sum_boostAxis_lightConeCoeff
declarations.doc:
**The light-cone directions are eigenvectors of the boost.** Along the `i`-th axis
`D₀ - Dᵢ` is scaled by `t²`, `D₀ + Dᵢ` by `t⁻²`, and the two transverse directions are
fixed.

    {t : ℝ} (ht : t ≠ 0) :
    ∑ μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3,
        (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup (SL2C.boostAxis i t ht)).1 ν μ : ℝ) : ℂ) * lightConeCoeff i κ μ
      = ((t : ℝ) : ℂ) ^ (lightConeWeight κ) * lightConeCoeff i κ ν

declarations.doc:

half-sum and half-difference of `D₀ ∓ Dᵢ`, and the transverse directions are themselves.

declarations.doc: The light-cone basis is a basis: the two coefficient matrices are inverse.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_lightConeCoeffInv_mul (i : Fin 3) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    ∑ κ : Fin 4, lightConeCoeffInv i μ κ * lightConeCoeff i κ ν = if μ = ν then 1 else 0

declarations.name: Lorentz.sum_prod_lightConeCoeff
declarations.doc:
The scalar behind `lightConeDeriv_mem`: the boost acts on a light-cone multi-index
slot by slot, so the product of the per-slot eigenvalues factors out.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_prod_lightConeCoeff (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → Fin 4)
    (a : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) {t : ℝ} (ht : t ≠ 0) :
    ∑ d : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, (∏ j, lightConeCoeff i (c j) (d j)) *
        (∏ j, (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup (SL2C.boostAxis i t ht)).1 (a j) (d j) : ℝ) : ℂ))
      = ((t : ℝ) : ℂ) ^ (∑ j, lightConeWeight (c j)) * ∏ j, lightConeCoeff i (c j) (a j)

declarations.name: Lorentz.sum_prod_lightConeCoeffInv
declarations.doc:
The two coefficient matrices are inverse slot by slot, hence inverse on multi-indices;
this is `sum_prod_lightConeCoeff` with the two factors the other way round.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_prod_lightConeCoeffInv (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ} (d e : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    ∑ c : Fin n → Fin 4, (∏ j, lightConeCoeffInv i (d j) (c j)) *
        (∏ j, lightConeCoeff i (c j) (e j)) = if d = e then 1 else 0

modules.title: The defining relation of the Lorentz group on its entries
modules.doc:
The relation `Λ η Λᵀ = η` over `ℂ`, read on a single entry and with integer metric entries.

## i. Overview

`Physlib.Relativity.LorentzGroup.Basic` states the defining relation of the Lorentz group as
the matrix equation `Λ η Λᵀ = η` over `ℝ`. A classification of invariant tensors contracts
that relation one metric pairing at a time, over `ℂ` and against entries which a decision
procedure has to evaluate. `sum_minkowskiMatrixZ_mul` is the relation in exactly that form:
the entry `(a, b)`, the coefficients cast into `ℂ`, and the metric entries taken from
`minkowskiMatrixZ` rather than `minkowskiMatrix`.

## ii. Key results

- `LorentzGroup.sum_minkowskiMatrixZ_mul` : the defining relation on the entry `(a, b)`, over
  `ℂ` and with integer metric entries.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The defining relation on an entry

## iv. References

The defining relation and its matrix forms are in `Physlib.Relativity.LorentzGroup.Basic`.

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.sum_minkowskiMatrixZ_mul
declarations.doc:
The defining relation `Λ η Λᵀ = η` over `ℂ`, read on the entry `(a, b)` and with the

classifications contract against, one metric pairing per pair of slots.

modules.title: Fermionic parity
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The homomorphism `SL(2, ℂ) → LorentzGroup 3` is two-to-one, and the nontrivial element of its
kernel is `-1`. Physically it is the rotation by `2π`: it acts as the identity on every tensor,
and as `-1` on every spinor, so it measures the parity of the number of fermionic indices
carried by a quantity. We call it the *fermionic parity*.

Because it lies in the Lorentz group's double cover and projects to the identity, any quantity
required to be invariant under `SL(2, ℂ)` is fixed by it. A quantity carrying an odd number of
spinor indices is negated by it, and therefore vanishes: this is the selection rule that forbids
terms with an odd number of fermions.

## ii. Key results

- `LorentzGroup.fermionicParity` : the nontrivial element of the kernel of the covering
  `SL(2, ℂ) → LorentzGroup 3`.
- `LorentzGroup.toSelfAdjointMap_fermionicParity` : it acts trivially on self-adjoint matrices.
- `LorentzGroup.toLorentzGroup_fermionicParity` : it projects to the identity Lorentz
  transformation.
- `LorentzGroup.fermionicParity_sq` : it squares to one.
- `LorentzGroup.fermionicParity_ne_one` : it is not itself the identity.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Fermionic parity
- B. The action on vectors and on spinors

## iv. References

* None.

## B. The action on vectors and on spinors

Fermionic parity is invisible on Lorentz vectors and acts by `-1` on Weyl spinors: this is what
makes it measure the parity of the number of spinor indices.

modules.title: The colours of complex Lorentz tensors are closed under adjoints
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A family of vectors in a representation `repLorentz` of `SL(2,ℂ)` on `B`, carrying Lorentz
indices of colours `c`, is packaged as a linear map `f : ℂT(c) →ₗ[ℂ] B`, equivariant in the sense
`complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant c repLorentz f`. The invariants in the range of such a map
come from invariant tensors whenever the colours are closed under adjoints,
`TensorSpecies.IsAdjointClosed`.

For `SL(2,ℂ)` this follows from each colour being dagger compatible: in its basis, the matrix of
`g†` is the conjugate transpose of the matrix of `g`. This holds for all six colours (B), so
every list of colours is closed under adjoints, `complexLorentzTensor.isAdjointClosed`.

## ii. Key results

- `Lorentz.IsDaggerCompatible` : the matrix of `g†` is the conjugate transpose of that of `g`.
- `Lorentz.isDaggerCompatible` : every colour is dagger compatible.
- `complexLorentzTensor.isAdjointClosed` : every list of colours is closed under adjoints.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The matrices of the colours
- B. Dagger-compatible colours

## iv. References

modules.title: Invariant coefficient tensors on spacetime indices
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The invariants in the range of an equivariant map out of the complex Lorentz tensors with `n`
contravariant indices are the images of invariant tensors, and the components of a tensor,
relabelled by `Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3` in each slot, are a coefficient tensor on which `SL(2,ℂ)` acts by
`act` (`Invariants.LorentzCovariance`). This file holds the machinery the rank-specific files use
to classify the invariant coefficient tensors, `IsInvariantCoeff`.

A matrix `M` acts on coefficient functions by `actMat M`, and a covector that the transposed
matrix reproduces up to a scalar reads off a component that `actMat M` scales by that scalar, so
an invariant coefficient function has no such component unless the scalar is `1` (A). Writing
each slot of a coefficient tensor in the light-cone basis of an axis splits it into pieces that
a boost scales by powers of its parameter, and an invariant keeps only the piece of weight zero:
`IsInvariantCoeff.lightConeComponent_eq_zero` (B). Section C records what the half turns about the
axes and the cyclic rotation of the axes force on an invariant coefficient tensor, for any number
of slots.

The conjugate transpose `dagger g` of an element of `SL(2,ℂ)`, whose Lorentz matrix is the
transpose of that of `g`, also lives here; it makes the colours of complex Lorentz tensors closed
under adjoints (`Invariants.AdjointClosed`).

## ii. Key results

- `Lorentz.Invariants.IsInvariantCoeff` : invariant coefficient tensors.
- `Lorentz.Invariants.IsInvariantCoeff.lightConeComponent_eq_zero` : the boost kills the
  light-cone components of nonzero weight.
- `Lorentz.Invariants.dagger` : the conjugate transpose in `SL(2,ℂ)`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Coefficient functions moved by a matrix
- B. Coefficient tensors on spacetime indices
- C. The half turns and the cyclic rotation

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. Coefficient functions moved by a matrix

A matrix `M` acts on coefficient functions by `actMat M`. The weight argument is generic: a
covector that the transposed matrix reproduces up to a scalar reads off a component that
`actMat M` scales by that scalar, so an invariant coefficient function has no such component
unless the scalar is `1`.
## B. Coefficient tensors on spacetime indices

## C. The half turns and the cyclic rotation

The half turn `SL2C.halfTurn k` has a diagonal Lorentz matrix with the signs `halfTurnSign k`,
so it multiplies the coefficient at `d` by the product of the signs of the slots of `d`. That
product is `1` or `-1`, and where it is `-1` invariance forces the coefficient to vanish.

The cyclic rotation `SL2C.rotationCycle` has the permutation matrix of `cycDir`, so it moves
coefficients rather than rescaling them, and invariance says that a coefficient tensor takes
the same value at `d` and at `cycIdx d`, the index vector with every slot rotated.

declarations.name: Lorentz.Invariants.lightConeComponent_act
declarations.doc:
A light-cone multi-index that `Λ` reproduces up to a scalar `k` has its light-cone
component scaled by `k`. The hypothesis is the eigenvector equation for the covector
`∏ₛ lightConeCoeff i (κ s) (·)` under the transposed action, which is the form the light-cone
directions of an axis satisfy for the transformations diagonal in that basis: the boost along
the axis, with `k` a power of its parameter, and the half turn about it, with `k` the product
of the signs of the slots.
declarations.statement:
lemma lightConeComponent_act (i : Fin 3) (Λ : Matrix (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) ℝ)
    (c : (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ) (κ : Fin n → Fin 4) (k : ℂ)
    (hΛ : ∀ d : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3,
      ∑ a : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, (∏ s, lightConeCoeff i (κ s) (a s))
          * ∏ s, ((Λ (a s) (d s) : ℝ) : ℂ)
        = k * ∏ s, lightConeCoeff i (κ s) (d s)) :
    lightConeComponent i (act Λ c) κ = k * lightConeComponent i c κ

modules.title: Lorentz invariants of a half-integer spin
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The other files of this folder classify the invariants of a given index pattern by contracting
the components with a coefficient tensor. This one settles, in one step and for every pattern
at once, the patterns that carry no invariant for the crudest of reasons: they are of
half-integer spin, and a half-integer spin has no invariant because the centre of `SL(2,ℂ)`
already tells integer spin from half-integer spin apart.

The element `-1` of `SL(2,ℂ)` covers the identity Lorentz transformation
(`SL2C.toLorentzGroup_neg_one`), so a representation of `SL(2,ℂ)` that factors through the
Lorentz group — a tensor of four-vector indices — sends it to the identity, while each Weyl
index contributes a sign. A subspace with an odd number of Weyl indices therefore lies in the
`-1` eigenspace of `repLorentz (-1)`, and a vector both fixed by the group and negated by `-1`
is zero. `centreEigenspace` names the eigenspace, `mul_le_centreEigenspace` multiplies the two
signs in a product of subspaces, and `mem_of_invariant_of_mem_sup_centreEigenspace_neg_one` is
the classification modulo a Lorentz-stable subspace `S`, the form the Standard Model files use.

The subspaces that arise there are spans of symbol families, so section B reads the sign of
such a span off the sign of the value space: the covariant-derivative slots of a family
obeying `IsLorentzCovDerivTransforms` are inert at the centre, and only the value index moves.

The argument uses the central element alone: it needs neither a grading nor a light-cone
basis.

## ii. Key results

- `centreEigenspace` : the subspace on which the centre of `SL(2,ℂ)` acts by the scalar `ε`: an
  integer spin sits at `ε = 1` and a half-integer spin at `ε = -1`
- `mul_le_centreEigenspace` : the sign of a product is the product of the signs
- `mem_of_invariant_of_mem_sup_centreEigenspace_neg_one` : a subspace of half-integer spin carries
  no Lorentz invariant beyond a Lorentz-stable submodule `S`: an invariant of the join with `S`
  already lies in `S`

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The sign a subspace carries at the centre
- B. The sign of a symbol family
- C. Signs multiply
- D. The classification modulo a Lorentz-stable submodule

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The sign a subspace carries at the centre

The centre of `SL(2,ℂ)` is `±1` and squares to the identity, so `repLorentz (-1)` is an
involution and the only signs on offer are `±1`. A tensor of four-vector indices carries `1`,
a Weyl index carries `-1`, and nothing else is needed of the pattern.

## B. The sign of a symbol family

A family of symbols transforming as the covariant derivatives of a field valued in `V` carries
at the centre the sign that `V` does. The derivative slots mix by the Lorentz matrix, which is
the identity at the centre, so they contribute nothing; the value index moves by `rep.dual`,
which carries the sign of `rep` by section A. Both signs that occur are recorded, `ε = 1` for
the Lorentz-scalar value spaces and `ε = -1` for the Weyl ones.

## C. Signs multiply

The Lorentz action on the field algebra is by algebra maps, so the sign a product carries is
the product of the signs of its factors. This is the whole of the bookkeeping: two Weyl
indices cancel and an odd number does not.

## D. The classification modulo a Lorentz-stable submodule

A vector of a subspace of sign `-1` that the group fixes is negated by `-1` and fixed by it at
once, so it is zero. Modulo a stable subspace `S` this is the case `μ = -1` of
`reducesInvariantsTo_bot_of_apply_eq_smul`: the invariance leaves `-2` times the vector inside
`S`, and dividing by `-2` is allowed over `ℂ`; no quotient representation is needed.

declarations.name: Lorentz.Invariants.centreEigenspace
declarations.doc:

declarations.name: Lorentz.Invariants.mem_centreEigenspace
declarations.doc: Membership of `centreEigenspace` unfolded: the centre scales the vector by `ε`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_centreEigenspace {repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) V} {ε : ℂ} {x : V} :
    x ∈ centreEigenspace repLorentz ε ↔ repLorentz (-1) x = ε • x

declarations.name: Lorentz.Invariants.dual_neg_one_eq_smul_id
declarations.doc:
Dualising a representation preserves the sign at the centre: `-1` is its own inverse, so
the contragredient action of the centre is the transpose of a scalar.
declarations.statement:
lemma dual_neg_one_eq_smul_id {rep : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) V} {ε : ℂ}
    (hrep : rep (-1) = ε • LinearMap.id) : rep.dual (-1) = ε • LinearMap.id

declarations.doc:

declarations.name: Lorentz.Invariants.mul_le_centreEigenspace
declarations.doc: The sign of a product is the product of the signs.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_le_centreEigenspace {repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) A}
    (hmul : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (x y : A), repLorentz Λ (x * y) = repLorentz Λ x * repLorentz Λ y)
    {W₁ W₂ : Submodule ℂ A} {ε₁ ε₂ : ℂ} (h₁ : W₁ ≤ centreEigenspace repLorentz ε₁)
    (h₂ : W₂ ≤ centreEigenspace repLorentz ε₂) :
    W₁ * W₂ ≤ centreEigenspace repLorentz (ε₁ * ε₂)

declarations.name: Lorentz.Invariants.mem_of_invariant_of_mem_sup_centreEigenspace_neg_one
declarations.doc:
A subspace of half-integer spin carries no Lorentz invariant beyond a Lorentz-stable
submodule `S`: an invariant of the join with `S` already lies in `S`. The centre acts on the
subspace by `-1 ≠ 1`, so it reduces to `⊥`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_invariant_of_mem_sup_centreEigenspace_neg_one
    {repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) A} {W : Submodule ℂ A}
    (hW : W ≤ centreEigenspace repLorentz (-1)) (S : Submodule ℂ A)
    (hS : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) {x : A} (hx : x ∈ W ⊔ S)
    (hinv : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x) : x ∈ S

modules.title: Lorentz invariants of two Weyl indices of the same kind
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

Let `k` be one of the four Weyl colours and `f : ℂT[k, k] →ₗ[ℂ] B` a Lorentz-equivariant linear
map. Every Lorentz invariant in the range of `f` is a multiple of `f (metricTensor k)`, the
image of the `ε` metric of that colour, the shape of a Majorana or Dirac mass term. That is
`exists_smul_map_metricTensor_add_of_invariant`, stated modulo a
Lorentz-stable submodule `S`, and packaged for the reductions of the Standard Model as
`invariantReductionToMetricTensor`. The families with two left-handed,
two right-handed, two dual left-handed and two dual right-handed indices are `IsBiLeftWeyl`,
`IsBiRightWeyl`, `IsBiDualLeftWeyl` and `IsBiDualRightWeyl` (A).

By `TensorSpecies.IsEquivariant.invariantReductionToSpan` it is enough to show that the invariant
tensors of `ℂT[k, k]` are the multiples of `metricTensor k` (B). Two elements of `SL(2,ℂ)` pin
the components `r` of an invariant tensor down. The first acts on the colour `k` by
`diag (2, 2⁻¹)`, which scales `r (0, 0)` by `4` and `r (1, 1)` by `4⁻¹`, so these vanish. The
second acts by an antidiagonal matrix with entries `μ`, `μ² = -1`, which sends `r (0, 1)` to
`μ² r (1, 0)`, so `r (0, 1) = -r (1, 0)`. For `k = upL` these are the boost along `z` and the
half turn about `x`; for the other colours they are their images under conjugation and inversion.
The metric is itself invariant, with a nonzero `(0, 1)` component, so `r` is a multiple of its
components.

## ii. Key results

- `IsBiLeftWeyl` : a family with two left-handed Weyl indices `T^{α₁ α₂}`: an equivariant linear map
  out of `ℂT[.upL, .upL]`
- `IsBiRightWeyl` : a family with two right-handed Weyl indices `T^{α̇₁ α̇₂}`: an equivariant linear
  map out of `ℂT[.upR, .upR]`
- `IsBiDualLeftWeyl` : a family with two dual left-handed Weyl indices `T_{α₁ α₂}`: an equivariant
  linear map out of `ℂT[.downL, .downL]`
- `IsBiDualRightWeyl` : a family with two dual right-handed Weyl indices `T_{α̇₁ α̇₂}`: an
  equivariant linear map out of `ℂT[.downR, .downR]`
- `invariantReductionToMetricTensor`
- `exists_smul_map_metricTensor_add_of_invariant` : for a Weyl colour `k` and an equivariant map `f`
  out of `ℂT[k, k]`, every Lorentz invariant of `LinearMap.range f ⊔ S`, for `S` a Lorentz-stable
  submodule, is a multiple of the image `f (metricTensor k)` of the metric plus an element of `S`

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Families with two Weyl indices of the same kind
- B. The invariant tensors with two Weyl indices of the same kind
- C. The classification of the invariants
- D. Maps from components

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: Lorentz.basis_repr_smul_pair
declarations.doc:
The components of `g • t` for a tensor with two indices: the matrix of `g` in the colour of
each index acts on that index.
declarations.statement:
lemma basis_repr_smul_pair (g : SL(2,ℂ)) (t : ℂT[k, k']) (a : basisIdx k)
    (b : basisIdx k') :
    (Tensor.basis ![k, k']).repr (g • t)
        ((piFinTwoEquiv fun j : Fin 2 => basisIdx (![k, k'] j)).symm (a, b))
      = ∑ x, ∑ y, LinearMap.toMatrix (complexLorentzTensor.basis k)
          (complexLorentzTensor.basis k) (complexLorentzTensor.rep k g) a x *
        LinearMap.toMatrix (complexLorentzTensor.basis k') (complexLorentzTensor.basis k')
          (complexLorentzTensor.rep k' g) b y *
        (Tensor.basis ![k, k']).repr t
          ((piFinTwoEquiv fun j : Fin 2 => basisIdx (![k, k'] j)).symm (x, y))

declarations.name: Lorentz.basis_repr_pair_eq_neg_swap_of_invariant
declarations.doc:
The components of an invariant tensor with two Weyl indices of the same colour are
antisymmetric. The inverse boost along `z` scales the two diagonal components by `4` and `4⁻¹`,
and the inverse half turn about `x` sends the mixed component `(0, 1)` to minus `(1, 0)`; for
the dual colours the inverse cancels against the inverse in the matrix of the colour.
declarations.statement:
lemma basis_repr_pair_eq_neg_swap_of_invariant
    (hk : k = .upL ∨ k = .downL ∨ k = .upR ∨ k = .downR) {t : ℂT[k, k]}
    (ht : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), g • t = t) (a b : basisIdx k) :
    (Tensor.basis ![k, k]).repr t
        ((piFinTwoEquiv fun j : Fin 2 => basisIdx (![k, k] j)).symm (a, b))
      = - (Tensor.basis ![k, k]).repr t
        ((piFinTwoEquiv fun j : Fin 2 => basisIdx (![k, k] j)).symm (b, a))

declarations.doc:

metric does not vanish.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_eq_smul_metricTensor_of_invariant

    (ht : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), g • t = t) : ∃ a : ℂ, t = a • metricTensor k

declarations.doc:
For a Weyl colour `k` and an equivariant map `f` out of `ℂT[k, k]`, every Lorentz invariant

declarations.statement:
lemma exists_smul_map_metricTensor_add_of_invariant
    (hk : k = .upL ∨ k = .downL ∨ k = .upR ∨ k = .downR)
    (hf : complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant ![k, k] repLorentz f) (S : Submodule ℂ B)

declarations.name: Lorentz.ofPairComponents_mem
declarations.doc:
The image of `ofPairComponents T` lies in every submodule containing the vectors
`T a b`.
declarations.statement:
lemma ofPairComponents_mem (T : basisIdx k → basisIdx k' → B) {M : Submodule ℂ B}
    (hT : ∀ a b, T a b ∈ M) (t : ℂT[k, k']) : ofPairComponents T t ∈ M

declarations.name: Lorentz.map_ofPairComponents
declarations.doc:
A linear map applied after `ofPairComponents T` is `ofPairComponents` of its values on the
components.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_ofPairComponents {B' : Type*} [AddCommGroup B'] [Module ℂ B'] (σ : B →ₗ[ℂ] B')
    (T : basisIdx k → basisIdx k' → B) (t : ℂT[k, k']) :
    σ (ofPairComponents T t) = ofPairComponents (fun a b => σ (T a b)) t

declarations.name: Lorentz.ofPairComponents_sum
declarations.doc: `ofPairComponents` of a sum of families is the sum of the maps.
declarations.statement:
lemma ofPairComponents_sum {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι)
    (T : ι → basisIdx k → basisIdx k' → B) :
    ofPairComponents (fun a b => ∑ i ∈ s, T i a b) = ∑ i ∈ s, ofPairComponents (T i)

declarations.name: Lorentz.ofPairComponents_sub
declarations.doc: `ofPairComponents` of a difference of families is the difference of the maps.
declarations.statement:
lemma ofPairComponents_sub (T T' : basisIdx k → basisIdx k' → B) :
    ofPairComponents (fun a b => T a b - T' a b) = ofPairComponents T - ofPairComponents T'

declarations.name: Lorentz.isEquivariant_ofPairComponents
declarations.doc:
`ofPairComponents T` is equivariant when each index of `T a b` is moved by the matrix of `g`
in its colour, the summed index first in each factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_ofPairComponents {repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) B}
    (T : basisIdx k → basisIdx k' → B)
    (hT : ∀ (g : SL(2,ℂ)) a b, repLorentz g (T a b)
      = ∑ x, ∑ y, (LinearMap.toMatrix (complexLorentzTensor.basis k)
          (complexLorentzTensor.basis k) (complexLorentzTensor.rep k g) x a *
        LinearMap.toMatrix (complexLorentzTensor.basis k') (complexLorentzTensor.basis k')
          (complexLorentzTensor.rep k' g) y b) • T x y) :
    complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant ![k, k'] repLorentz (ofPairComponents T)

modules.title: Lorentz invariants of a left-handed and a right-handed Weyl index
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A bispinor `T^{α α'}`, carrying one left-handed and one right-handed Weyl index, has no Lorentz
invariant but `0`: the pair carries the `(1/2, 1/2)` representation, a single four-vector index,
which has nothing to contract with. The same holds for the dual pair `T_{α α'}`. The families are
equivariant linear maps out of `ℂT[.upL, .upR]` and `ℂT[.downL, .downR]`, `IsLeftRightWeyl` and
`IsDualLeftRightWeyl` (A).

By `TensorSpecies.IsEquivariant.reducesInvariantsTo_bot` it is enough that the only invariant
tensor is zero (B). Two diagonal elements of `SL(2,ℂ)` already force this. A diagonal
`g = diag (λ₀, λ₁)` multiplies the component `(a₁, a₂)` of a tensor of `ℂT[.upL, .upR]` by
`λ_{a₁} * conj λ_{a₂}`, and that of a tensor of `ℂT[.downL, .downR]` by the inverse of this. The
boost `diag (2, 2⁻¹)` along `z` scales `(0, 0)` by `4` and `(1, 1)` by `4⁻¹`, so these vanish,
and the half turn `diag (-i, i)` about `z` multiplies `(0, 1)` and `(1, 0)` by `-1`, so these
vanish too (C).

## ii. Key results

- `Lorentz.eq_zero_of_invariant_leftRight` : an invariant tensor with a left- and a
  right-handed Weyl index is zero.
- `Lorentz.IsLeftRightWeyl.reducesInvariantsTo_bot` : the invariants of the range of a
  left-right family reduce to `⊥`.
- `Lorentz.IsDualLeftRightWeyl.reducesInvariantsTo_bot` : the same for the dual indices.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Left-right families as equivariant maps
- B. The invariant tensors vanish
- C. The classification of the invariants

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: Lorentz invariants of a four-vector index and a left-right Weyl pair
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A family `T^{μ α α'}` carrying one four-vector index and one opposite-chirality Weyl pair is an
equivariant linear map `f : ℂT[.up, .upL, .upR] →ₗ[ℂ] B`, `IsVectorLeftRightWeyl` (A). Every
Lorentz invariant in the range of `f` is a multiple of `f σ^^^`, the image of the Pauli
matrices as a tensor, the shape of the fermion kinetic term `ψ̄_{α'} σ̄^{μ α' α} ∂_μ ψ_α`. That is
`IsVectorLeftRightWeyl.exists_smul_map_pauliMatrix_add_of_invariant`, stated modulo a
Lorentz-stable submodule `S`, and packaged as `IsVectorLeftRightWeyl.invariantReductionToSpan`
(D).

An opposite-chirality Weyl pair carries the `(1/2, 1/2)` representation, which is the
four-vector representation, so the three indices are two four-vector indices, and two of those
admit only the metric. The proof makes that literal. The components `f (e_μ ⊗ e_α ⊗ e_α')` of `f`
move as `T^{μ α α'}` (B); contracting their Weyl pair against the covariant Pauli matrices
`PauliMatrix.pauliLower`, which intertwine the two index laws (`SL2C.sum_pauliLower_mul_sl2c`),
gives a family `vectorPair f` of two four-vector indices, whose map is equivariant, whose range
is the range of `f` by Fierz completeness, and which sends the metric to `f σ^^^` (C); `RankTwo`
supplies the classification (D). A family of components is turned back into a map by
`ofVectorComponents` (E).

The Standard Model's fermion symbols are `Module.Dual`-valued, so their spinor indices are dual
Weyl indices: an equivariant map out of `ℂT[.up, .downR, .downL]`, `IsVectorDualLeftRightWeyl`.
Dualising both Weyl indices, `dualWeylMap`, is an equivariant surjection from
`ℂT[.up, .upL, .upR]` carrying `σ^^^` to `σ^__`, so every invariant in the range of such a map is
a multiple of `f σ^__` (F). A family of dual components is turned into a map by
`ofDualVectorComponents` (G).

## ii. Key results

- `Lorentz.IsVectorLeftRightWeyl.invariantReductionToSpan` : the invariants reduce to `f σ^^^`.
- `Lorentz.dualWeylMap` : the dualisation of the Weyl indices.
- `Lorentz.IsVectorDualLeftRightWeyl.invariantReductionToSpan` : the invariants reduce to
  `f σ^__`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Vector-Weyl families as equivariant maps
- B. The components of an equivariant map
- C. The reduction to a pair of four-vector indices
- D. The classification of the Lorentz invariants
- E. Maps from components
- F. Dual Weyl indices
- G. Maps from dual components

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Vector-Weyl families as equivariant maps

## B. The components of an equivariant map

The components `f (e_μ ⊗ e_α ⊗ e_α')` of an equivariant map are moved by the Lorentz matrix on
the vector index, by the matrix of `g` on the left Weyl index and by its complex conjugate on
the right one.

## C. The reduction to a pair of four-vector indices

Contracting the Weyl pair of the components against the covariant Pauli matrices gives a
family `vectorPair f` of two four-vector indices, whose map `ofComponents (vectorPair f)` is a
rank-two Lorentz family. By Fierz completeness the contraction is invertible, so its span is the
range of `f`, and the image of the metric under its map is `f σ^^^`.

## D. The classification of the Lorentz invariants

`RankTwo` classifies the invariants of the range of `ofComponents (vectorPair f)`, which is the
range of `f`, and the image of the metric under it is `f σ^^^`.

## E. Maps from components

A family `T (μ, α, α')` of vectors is the linear map `ofVectorComponents T` sending
`e_μ ⊗ e_α ⊗ e_α'` to `T (μ, α, α')`, and it is equivariant when the vectors are moved as the
basis tensors are.

## F. Dual Weyl indices

A family `T^μ{}_{α' α}` with a four-vector index and a dual right- and a dual left-handed Weyl
index is an equivariant map out of `ℂT[.up, .downR, .downL]`, `IsVectorDualLeftRightWeyl`.
Dualising both Weyl indices, `dualWeylMap`, is an equivariant surjection out of
`ℂT[.up, .upL, .upR]` which carries `σ^^^` to `σ^__`, so composing with it turns such a family
into an `IsVectorLeftRightWeyl` family with the same range, and section D applies.

## G. Maps from dual components

A family `T (μ, α, α')` of vectors, indexed by a four-vector index, a dual left-handed and a
dual right-handed Weyl index, is the linear map `ofDualVectorComponents T` sending
`e_μ ⊗ e_α' ⊗ e_α` to `T (μ, α, α')`, and it is equivariant when the vectors are moved as the
basis tensors are.

declarations.name: Lorentz.IsVectorLeftRightWeyl
declarations.doc:
A family with a four-vector index and a left- and a right-handed Weyl index `T^{μ α α'}`:
an equivariant linear map out of `ℂT[.up, .upL, .upR]`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsVectorLeftRightWeyl (B : Type*) [AddCommMonoid B] [Module ℂ B]
    (repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) B) (f : ℂT[.up, .upL, .upR] →ₗ[ℂ] B) : Prop

declarations.name: Lorentz.IsVectorLeftRightWeyl.repLorentz_map_indexBasis
declarations.doc:
The components of an equivariant map are moved as `T^{μ α α'}`, the summed index first in
each factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_map_indexBasis (g : SL(2,ℂ)) (d : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) × Fin 2 × Fin 2) :
    repLorentz g (f (indexBasis d)) = ∑ e : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) × Fin 2 × Fin 2,
      ((((SL2C.toLorentzGroup g).1 e.1 d.1 : ℝ) : ℂ)
        * (g.1 e.2.1 d.2.1 * star (g.1 e.2.2 d.2.2))) • f (indexBasis e)

declarations.name: Lorentz.IsVectorLeftRightWeyl.repLorentz_sum_smul
declarations.doc:
Moving a contraction of the Weyl pair at vector index `μ`: the vector index moves by the
Lorentz matrix and the coefficients of the Weyl pair by the matrix of `g` and its complex
conjugate.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_sum_smul (g : SL(2,ℂ)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (c : Fin 2 × Fin 2 → ℂ) :
    repLorentz g (∑ a : Fin 2 × Fin 2, c a • f (indexBasis (μ, a)))
      = ∑ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup g).1 ν μ : ℝ) : ℂ)
        • ∑ q : Fin 2 × Fin 2, (∑ d : Fin 2 × Fin 2, c d * (g.1 q.1 d.1 * star (g.1 q.2 d.2)))
          • f (indexBasis (ν, q))

declarations.name: Lorentz.IsVectorLeftRightWeyl.vectorPair
declarations.doc:
The family of two four-vector indices obtained by contracting the Weyl pair of the
components of `f` against the covariant Pauli matrices.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def vectorPair (f : ℂT[.up, .upL, .upR] →ₗ[ℂ] B) :
    (Fin 2 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B

declarations.name: Lorentz.IsVectorLeftRightWeyl.isLorentzCovariant_vectorPair
declarations.doc:
The reduced family is a rank-two Lorentz family: the intertwining identity
`SL2C.sum_pauliLower_mul_sl2c` carries the Weyl pair into a second vector index.
declarations.statement:
lemma isLorentzCovariant_vectorPair :
    IsLorentzCovariant 2 B repLorentz (ofComponents (vectorPair f))

declarations.name: Lorentz.IsVectorLeftRightWeyl.map_indexBasis_eq_sum_vectorPair
declarations.doc:
The reduction is invertible: by the Fierz completeness relation each component of `f` is
recovered from the reduced family.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_indexBasis_eq_sum_vectorPair (f : ℂT[.up, .upL, .upR] →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (b : Fin 2 × Fin 2) :
    f (indexBasis (μ, b)) = ∑ ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3,
      ((2 : ℂ)⁻¹ * PauliMatrix.pauliLower ρ b.2 b.1) • vectorPair f ![μ, ρ]

declarations.name: Lorentz.IsVectorLeftRightWeyl.span_range_vectorPair
declarations.doc: The reduction does not change the span: the reduced family spans the range of `f`.
declarations.statement:
lemma span_range_vectorPair (f : ℂT[.up, .upL, .upR] →ₗ[ℂ] B) :
    Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range (vectorPair f)) = LinearMap.range f

declarations.name: Lorentz.IsVectorLeftRightWeyl.ofComponents_vectorPair_metric
declarations.doc:
The image of the metric under the map of the reduced family is the image `f σ^^^` of the
Pauli tensor: the two lowerings of the vector index cancel, so no sign and no scalar appear.
declarations.statement:
lemma ofComponents_vectorPair_metric (f : ℂT[.up, .upL, .upR] →ₗ[ℂ] B) :
    ofComponents (vectorPair f) RankTwo.metric = f σ^^^

declarations.name: Lorentz.IsVectorLeftRightWeyl.repLorentz_map_pauliMatrix
declarations.doc: The image `f σ^^^` of the Pauli tensor is Lorentz invariant.
declarations.statement: lemma repLorentz_map_pauliMatrix (g : SL(2,ℂ)) : repLorentz g (f σ^^^) = f σ^^^

declarations.name: Lorentz.IsVectorLeftRightWeyl.exists_smul_map_pauliMatrix_add_of_invariant
declarations.doc:
Every Lorentz invariant of `LinearMap.range f ⊔ S`, for `S` a Lorentz-stable submodule, is a
multiple of the image `f σ^^^` of the Pauli tensor plus an element of `S`: the shape of the
fermion kinetic term.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_smul_map_pauliMatrix_add_of_invariant (S : Submodule ℂ B)
    (hS : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) {x : B}
    (hx : x ∈ LinearMap.range f ⊔ S) (hinv : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x) :
    ∃ a : ℂ, ∃ y ∈ S, x = a • f σ^^^ + y

declarations.name: Lorentz.IsVectorLeftRightWeyl.invariantReductionToSpan
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz invariants of the range of `f` reduce to the span of the image `f σ^^^` of the
Pauli tensor.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def invariantReductionToSpan :
    InvariantReductionToSpan (fun g : SL(2,ℂ) => repLorentz g) (LinearMap.range f)

declarations.name: Lorentz.ofVectorComponents
declarations.doc:
The linear map out of `ℂT[.up, .upL, .upR]` sending `e_μ ⊗ e_α ⊗ e_α'` to
`T (μ, α, α')`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def ofVectorComponents (T : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) × Fin 2 × Fin 2 → B) :
    ℂT[.up, .upL, .upR] →ₗ[ℂ] B

declarations.name: Lorentz.ofVectorComponents_indexBasis
declarations.statement:
lemma ofVectorComponents_indexBasis (T : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) × Fin 2 × Fin 2 → B)
    (d : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) × Fin 2 × Fin 2) : ofVectorComponents T (indexBasis d) = T d

declarations.name: Lorentz.range_ofVectorComponents
declarations.doc: The range of `ofVectorComponents T` is the span of the vectors `T d`.
declarations.statement:
lemma range_ofVectorComponents (T : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) × Fin 2 × Fin 2 → B) :
    LinearMap.range (ofVectorComponents T) = Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range T)

declarations.name: Lorentz.isVectorLeftRightWeyl_ofVectorComponents
declarations.doc:
`ofVectorComponents T` is equivariant when `T (μ, α, α')` is moved as `T^{μ α α'}`: the
vector index by the Lorentz matrix, the left index by the matrix of `g` and the right index by
its complex conjugate, the summed index first in each factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma isVectorLeftRightWeyl_ofVectorComponents {repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) B}
    (T : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) × Fin 2 × Fin 2 → B)
    (hT : ∀ (g : SL(2,ℂ)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (l : Fin 2 × Fin 2),
      repLorentz g (T (μ, l)) = ∑ (ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3), ∑ (a : Fin 2 × Fin 2),
        ((((SL2C.toLorentzGroup g).1 ν μ : ℝ) : ℂ)
          * (g.1 a.1 l.1 * star (g.1 a.2 l.2))) • T (ν, a)) :
    IsVectorLeftRightWeyl B repLorentz (ofVectorComponents T)

declarations.name: Lorentz.IsVectorDualLeftRightWeyl
declarations.doc:
A family with a four-vector index and a dual right- and a dual left-handed Weyl index
`T^μ{}_{α' α}`: an equivariant linear map out of `ℂT[.up, .downR, .downL]`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsVectorDualLeftRightWeyl (B : Type*) [AddCommMonoid B] [Module ℂ B]
    (repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) B) (f : ℂT[.up, .downR, .downL] →ₗ[ℂ] B) : Prop

declarations.name: Lorentz.dualWeylMap
declarations.doc:
Dualising the two Weyl indices of a tensor with a four-vector index and a left-right Weyl
pair, the dual indices listed in the order of `σ^__`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def dualWeylMap : ℂT[.up, .upL, .upR] →ₗ[ℂ] ℂT[.up, .downR, .downL]

declarations.name: Lorentz.dualWeylMap_equivariant
declarations.doc: Dualising the Weyl indices commutes with the action of `SL(2,ℂ)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma dualWeylMap_equivariant (g : SL(2,ℂ)) (t : ℂT[.up, .upL, .upR]) :
    dualWeylMap (g • t) = g • dualWeylMap t

declarations.name: Lorentz.dualWeylMap_pauliMatrix
declarations.doc: Dualising the Weyl indices of `σ^^^` gives `σ^__`.
declarations.statement: lemma dualWeylMap_pauliMatrix : dualWeylMap σ^^^ = σ^__

declarations.name: Lorentz.dualWeylMap_surjective
declarations.doc:
Dualising the Weyl indices is surjective: the dualisations are inverted by raising the
indices again, and the relabelling by its inverse.
declarations.statement: lemma dualWeylMap_surjective : Function.Surjective dualWeylMap

declarations.name: Lorentz.IsVectorDualLeftRightWeyl.isVectorLeftRightWeyl_comp_dualWeylMap
declarations.doc:
Composing with the dualisation of the Weyl indices gives a family with a four-vector index
and a left-right Weyl pair.
declarations.statement:
lemma isVectorLeftRightWeyl_comp_dualWeylMap :
    IsVectorLeftRightWeyl B repLorentz (f ∘ₗ dualWeylMap)

declarations.name: Lorentz.IsVectorDualLeftRightWeyl.range_comp_dualWeylMap
declarations.doc: Composing with the dualisation of the Weyl indices does not change the range.
declarations.statement: lemma range_comp_dualWeylMap : LinearMap.range (f ∘ₗ dualWeylMap) = LinearMap.range f

declarations.name: Lorentz.IsVectorDualLeftRightWeyl.exists_smul_map_pauliContrDown_add_of_invariant
declarations.doc:
Every Lorentz invariant of `LinearMap.range f ⊔ S`, for `S` a Lorentz-stable submodule, is a
multiple of the image `f σ^__` of the Pauli tensor with dual Weyl indices plus an element of
`S`: the kinetic term of a Weyl fermion.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_smul_map_pauliContrDown_add_of_invariant (S : Submodule ℂ B)
    (hS : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) {x : B}
    (hx : x ∈ LinearMap.range f ⊔ S) (hinv : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x) :
    ∃ a : ℂ, ∃ y ∈ S, x = a • f σ^__ + y

declarations.name: Lorentz.IsVectorDualLeftRightWeyl.invariantReductionToSpan
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz invariants of the range of `f` reduce to the span of the image `f σ^__` of the
Pauli tensor with dual Weyl indices.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def invariantReductionToSpan :
    InvariantReductionToSpan (fun g : SL(2,ℂ) => repLorentz g) (LinearMap.range f)

declarations.name: Lorentz.dualIndexEquiv
declarations.doc:
The component indices of a tensor of `ℂT[.up, .downR, .downL]`, as a four-vector index, a
dual left-handed and a dual right-handed Weyl index.
declarations.statement:
def dualIndexEquiv : ComponentIdx (S := complexLorentzTensor) ![.up, .downR, .downL] ≃
    (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) × Fin 2 × Fin 2

declarations.name: Lorentz.ofDualVectorComponents
declarations.doc:
The linear map out of `ℂT[.up, .downR, .downL]` sending `e_μ ⊗ e_α' ⊗ e_α` to
`T (μ, α, α')`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def ofDualVectorComponents (T : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) × Fin 2 × Fin 2 → B) :
    ℂT[.up, .downR, .downL] →ₗ[ℂ] B

declarations.name: Lorentz.range_ofDualVectorComponents
declarations.doc: The range of `ofDualVectorComponents T` is the span of the vectors `T d`.
declarations.statement:
lemma range_ofDualVectorComponents (T : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) × Fin 2 × Fin 2 → B) :
    LinearMap.range (ofDualVectorComponents T) = Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range T)

declarations.name: Lorentz.ofDualVectorComponents_mem_span
declarations.doc: The image of `ofDualVectorComponents T` lies in the span of the vectors `T d`.
declarations.statement:
lemma ofDualVectorComponents_mem_span (T : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) × Fin 2 × Fin 2 → B)
    (t : ℂT[.up, .downR, .downL]) :
    ofDualVectorComponents T t ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range T)

declarations.name: Lorentz.ofDualVectorComponents_sum
declarations.doc: `ofDualVectorComponents` of a sum of families is the sum of the maps.
declarations.statement:
lemma ofDualVectorComponents_sum {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι)
    (T : ι → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) × Fin 2 × Fin 2 → B) :
    ofDualVectorComponents (fun d => ∑ i ∈ s, T i d) = ∑ i ∈ s, ofDualVectorComponents (T i)

declarations.name: Lorentz.isVectorDualLeftRightWeyl_ofDualVectorComponents
declarations.doc:
`ofDualVectorComponents T` is equivariant when `T (μ, α, α')` is moved as `T^μ{}_{α α'}`: the
vector index by the Lorentz matrix, the dual left index by `(g⁻¹)ᵀ` and the dual right index
by `(g⁻¹)ᴴ`, the summed index first in each factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma isVectorDualLeftRightWeyl_ofDualVectorComponents
    {repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) B} (T : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) × Fin 2 × Fin 2 → B)
    (hT : ∀ (g : SL(2,ℂ)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (l : Fin 2 × Fin 2),
      repLorentz g (T (μ, l)) = ∑ (ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3), ∑ (a : Fin 2 × Fin 2),
        ((((SL2C.toLorentzGroup g).1 ν μ : ℝ) : ℂ)
          * ((g.1⁻¹)ᵀ a.1 l.1 * (g.1⁻¹)ᴴ a.2 l.2)) • T (ν, a)) :
    IsVectorDualLeftRightWeyl B repLorentz (ofDualVectorComponents T)

declarations.name: Lorentz.IsVectorDualLeftRightWeyl.invariantReductionToComponentSpan
declarations.doc:
For a family whose map is equivariant, the Lorentz invariants of the span of the family
reduce to the span of the image `ofDualVectorComponents T σ^__` of the Pauli tensor with dual
Weyl indices.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def IsVectorDualLeftRightWeyl.invariantReductionToComponentSpan

modules.title: The light-cone basis of a boost axis over the integers
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

`lightConeCoeff` and `lightConeCoeffInv` of `LightConeDeriv` change a spacetime index into the
light-cone basis of a spatial axis `i`: the two directions `D₀ - Dᵢ` and `D₀ + Dᵢ` of the plane
the boost along `i` moves, and the two transverse directions. Their entries are `0`, `±1` and
`±1/2`, so both matrices have integer mirrors, and the rank-four classification computes with
them in the kernel, which evaluates `ℤ` and does not evaluate `ℂ`. This file holds the mirrors
and what is proved about them at an arbitrary number of indices.

The change of basis one way is `lightConeCoeffZ`, an exact integer copy. The other way needs
the halves, and `lightConeCoeffInvZ` clears them, so it is twice the true inverse and a
contraction over `n` slots carries a factor `2 ^ n` that the rank-four file divides out. That
is the only normalization in play, and `coe_lightConeCoeffInvZ_eq_two_mul` records it against
`ℂ`.

`InBoostPlane` separates the two directions of weight `±2` from the two transverse ones, one
index at a time. `slotZ` is one slot of the change of basis, and `transitionZ` composes it over
`n` slots into `2 ^ n` times the map keeping the light-cone components of total weight `m`;
`transitionZ_eq_sum` unfolds that recursion into a single sum over the multi-indices of that
weight.

## ii. Key results

- `lightConeCoeffZ` : the four light-cone directions of axis `i`, as integers
- `lightConeCoeffInvZ` : twice the coordinate directions in the light-cone basis, the `2` clearing
  the halves
- `coe_lightConeCoeffInvZ_eq_two_mul` : the integer copy is exactly twice `lightConeCoeffInv`
- `InBoostPlane` : the boost plane of axis `i`: time and the axis, the two directions the boost
  moves
- `slotZ` : one slot's factor: twice the coefficient of `κ` in `μ`, times that of `ν` in `κ`
- `transitionZ` : two to the number of slots times the entry, at `d` and `e`, of the map keeping the
  light-cone components of total weight `m` along axis `i`; the factor is the one
  `lightConeCoeffInvZ` carries, one per slot
- `transitionZ_eq_sum` : the recursion unfolded, as a sum over the multi-indices of total weight `m`

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The change of basis over the integers
- B. The boost plane
- C. The weight-keeping transition over any number of slots

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The change of basis over the integers

## B. The boost plane

The boost along axis `i` moves time and the axis and fixes the two transverse directions, so
the light-cone directions of weight `±2` are supported in the first pair and the two of weight
`0` in the second. Either half of that statement kills half of `lightConeCoeffInvZ`.

## C. The weight-keeping transition over any number of slots

One slot of the change of basis, keeping the four directions apart, is `slotZ`, and composing it
over `n` slots while tracking the weight left to distribute gives `transitionZ`. The recursion
follows B: a slot whose direction lies in the boost plane takes weight `2` or `-2` and leaves
`m - 2` or `m + 2`, and a transverse slot takes either direction of weight `0`, which is why
those two are added, and leaves `m`.

Unfolding the recursion into a single sum splits into two independent steps. The case split of
the recursion is the boost-plane support argument of B and nothing else: once it is resolved,
one slot is a plain sum over the four directions, each taking its own weight out of `m`
(`transitionZ_succ`). What is left has no light-cone content at all, the peeling of the first
slot off a weight-constrained sum over tuples, which is `Physlib.Fin.sum_filter_weight_succ`.
`transitionZ_eq_sum` is the induction that composes them.

declarations.doc: The four light-cone directions of axis `i`, as integers.

declarations.statement: def lightConeCoeffInvZ (i : Fin 3) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (κ : Fin 4) : ℤ

declarations.doc: The boost plane of axis `i`: time and the axis, the two directions the boost moves.
declarations.statement: def InBoostPlane (i : Fin 3) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : Prop
instance (i : Fin 3) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : Decidable (InBoostPlane i μ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.Invariants.lightConeCoeffInvZ_eq_zero_of_inBoostPlane
declarations.doc: A direction in the boost plane has no transverse light-cone components.

declarations.name: Lorentz.Invariants.lightConeCoeffInvZ_eq_zero_of_not_inBoostPlane
declarations.doc: A transverse direction has no light-cone components in the boost plane.

declarations.name: Lorentz.Invariants.slotZ
declarations.doc: One slot's factor: twice the coefficient of `κ` in `μ`, times that of `ν` in `κ`.
declarations.statement: def slotZ (i : Fin 3) (κ : Fin 4) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : ℤ

declarations.name: Lorentz.Invariants.transitionZ
declarations.doc:
Two to the number of slots times the entry, at `d` and `e`, of the map keeping the light-cone
components of total weight `m` along axis `i`; the factor is the one `lightConeCoeffInvZ`
carries, one per slot. A slot of `d` in the boost plane takes weight `2` or `-2`, leaving
`m - 2` or `m + 2`; a transverse slot takes weight `0` and leaves `m`.
declarations.statement: def transitionZ (i : Fin 3) : {n : ℕ} → (d e : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℤ → ℤ

declarations.name: Lorentz.Invariants.transitionZ_succ
declarations.doc:
One slot of the transition, with the case split of the recursion resolved: the first slot
runs over all four light-cone directions, each taking its own weight out of `m`. The two
directions of the boost plane drop out of a transverse slot and the two transverse ones drop
out of a slot in the boost plane, which is what the two branches of `transitionZ` record.
declarations.statement:
lemma transitionZ_succ (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ} (d e : Fin (n + 1) → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (m : ℤ) :
    transitionZ i d e m
      = ∑ κ : Fin 4, slotZ i κ (d 0) (e 0)
          * transitionZ i (Fin.tail d) (Fin.tail e) (m - lightConeWeight κ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.Invariants.transitionZ_eq_sum
declarations.doc: The recursion unfolded, as a sum over the multi-indices of total weight `m`.
declarations.statement:
lemma transitionZ_eq_sum (i : Fin 3) :
    ∀ {n : ℕ} (d e : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (m : ℤ),
    transitionZ i d e m
      = ∑ κ ∈ Finset.univ.filter
          (fun κ : Fin n → Fin 4 => (∑ s, lightConeWeight (κ s)) = m),
        ∏ s, slotZ i (κ s) (d s) (e s)

modules.title: Equivariant maps out of tensors with four-vector indices
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A family of vectors of a complex module `B`, indexed by `n` spacetime directions and moved by a
representation `repLorentz` of `SL(2,ℂ)` with one factor of the Lorentz matrix per index, is
packaged as a linear map `f` out of the complex Lorentz tensors with `n` contravariant indices,
and `IsLorentzCovariant n B repLorentz f` says that `f` is equivariant (A). The rank-specific
files of this folder classify the Lorentz invariants in the range of such a map.

The components of a tensor, relabelled by `Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3` in each slot, are a coefficient tensor,
`coeffEquiv` (B), on which `SL(2,ℂ)` acts by `Invariants.act`. An invariant tensor therefore has
an invariant coefficient tensor, `Invariants.IsInvariantCoeff`, and a classification of the
invariant coefficient tensors is a classification of the invariants in the range of `f` (C).

A family `T` of vectors indexed by `n` directions is the map `ofComponents T`, sending each basis
tensor to the matching vector, and it is equivariant exactly when the vectors obey the
transformation law of the components of a tensor (D),

`repLorentz g (T l) = ∑_a (∏ i, Λ(g)_{a i, l i}) • T a`,

with `l` free and `a` summed, and the summed index first in each factor of the Lorentz matrix
`Λ(g)` of `g`. Permuting the slots by `permT σ` reads the coefficient tensor and the family at
permuted index vectors (`permT_coeffEquiv_symm`, `ofComponents_comp_permT`).

## ii. Key results

- `Lorentz.IsLorentzCovariant` : equivariant maps out of tensors with `n` four-vector indices.
- `Lorentz.coeffEquiv` : the components of such a tensor, as a coefficient tensor.
- `Lorentz.invariant_iff_isInvariantCoeff` : a tensor is invariant exactly when its coefficient
  tensor is.
- `Lorentz.IsLorentzCovariant.reducesInvariantsTo_span` : a spanning set of the invariant
  coefficient tensors gives a reduction of the invariants of the range.
- `Lorentz.isLorentzCovariant_ofComponents_iff` : the map of a family is equivariant exactly when
  the family obeys the transformation law.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Equivariant maps
- B. Coefficient tensors
- C. The reduction to invariant coefficient tensors
- D. Maps from components

## iv. References

* None.
