declarations.name: Lorentz.IsLorentzCovariant
declarations.doc:
A family with `n` four-vector indices `T^{μ₁ ⋯ μₙ}` in a representation `repLorentz` of
`SL(2,ℂ)`: an equivariant linear map out of the complex Lorentz tensors with `n` contravariant
indices.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsLorentzCovariant (n : ℕ) (B : Type*) [AddCommMonoid B] [Module ℂ B]
    (repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) B)
    (f : ℂT(fun _ : Fin n => Color.up) →ₗ[ℂ] B) : Prop

declarations.name: Lorentz.sum_pi_fin_two
declarations.doc: A sum over families of two four-vector indices is a double sum.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_pi_fin_two {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] (f : (Fin 2 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M) :
    ∑ d : Fin 2 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, f d
      = ∑ x : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, ∑ y : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, f ![x, y]

declarations.name: Lorentz.vectorIdx
declarations.doc:
The component indices of a tensor with `n` contravariant indices, which are labelled by
`Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3` in each slot.

declarations.name: Lorentz.vectorIdx_symm_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma vectorIdx_symm_apply (d : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (i : Fin n) :
    (vectorIdx n).symm d i = d i

declarations.name: Lorentz.coeffEquiv
declarations.doc: The components of a tensor with `n` contravariant indices, as a coefficient tensor.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def coeffEquiv (n : ℕ) :
    ℂT(fun _ : Fin n => Color.up) ≃ₗ[ℂ] ((Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.coeffEquiv_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma coeffEquiv_apply (t : ℂT(fun _ : Fin n => Color.up)) (d : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    coeffEquiv n t d = (Tensor.basis _).repr t ((vectorIdx n).symm d)

declarations.name: Lorentz.coeffEquiv_symm_apply
declarations.doc:
The tensor with coefficient tensor `c` is the combination of the basis tensors with those
coefficients.
declarations.statement:
lemma coeffEquiv_symm_apply (c : (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ) :
    (coeffEquiv n).symm c = ∑ d, c d • Tensor.basis _ ((vectorIdx n).symm d)

declarations.name: Lorentz.permT_coeffEquiv_symm
declarations.doc:
Permuting the slots of a tensor by `σ` permutes its coefficient tensor: slot `i` of
`permT σ h t` holds slot `σ i` of `t`, so the new coefficient at `d` is the old one at
`d ∘ σ.symm`.
declarations.statement:
lemma permT_coeffEquiv_symm (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n))
    (h : IsReindexing (fun _ : Fin n => Color.up) (fun _ => Color.up) σ)
    (c : (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ) :
    permT σ h ((coeffEquiv n).symm c) = (coeffEquiv n).symm fun d => c (d ∘ σ.symm)

declarations.name: Lorentz.coeffEquiv_smul
declarations.doc:
The action of `g` on tensors is the action `act` of its Lorentz matrix on coefficient
tensors.
declarations.statement:
lemma coeffEquiv_smul (g : SL(2,ℂ)) (t : ℂT(fun _ : Fin n => Color.up)) :
    coeffEquiv n (g • t) = act (SL2C.toLorentzGroup g).1 (coeffEquiv n t)

declarations.name: Lorentz.invariant_iff_isInvariantCoeff
declarations.doc:
A tensor is invariant exactly when its coefficient tensor is an invariant coefficient
tensor.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariant_iff_isInvariantCoeff (t : ℂT(fun _ : Fin n => Color.up)) :
    (∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), g • t = t) ↔ IsInvariantCoeff (coeffEquiv n t)

declarations.name: Lorentz.IsLorentzCovariant.reducesInvariantsTo_span
declarations.doc:
When the invariant coefficient tensors lie in the span of the coefficient tensors `K j`, the
invariants of the range of `f` reduce to the span of the images of the tensors with those
coefficients.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_span (hf : IsLorentzCovariant n B repLorentz f) {ι : Type*}
    (K : ι → (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ)
    (hK : ∀ c, IsInvariantCoeff c → c ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range K)) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (fun g : SL(2,ℂ) => repLorentz g) (LinearMap.range f)
      (Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range fun j => f ((coeffEquiv n).symm (K j))))

declarations.name: Lorentz.IsLorentzCovariant.reducesInvariantsTo_bot_of_isInvariantCoeff
declarations.doc: When the only invariant coefficient tensor is zero, the range of `f` reduces to `⊥`.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_bot_of_isInvariantCoeff (hf : IsLorentzCovariant n B repLorentz f)
    (hK : ∀ c : (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ, IsInvariantCoeff c → c = 0) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (fun g : SL(2,ℂ) => repLorentz g) (LinearMap.range f) ⊥

declarations.name: Lorentz.IsLorentzCovariant.eq_zero_of_isInvariantCoeff
declarations.doc:
When the only invariant coefficient tensor is zero, so is every Lorentz invariant in the
range of `f`.

declarations.name: Lorentz.ofComponents
declarations.doc:
The linear map out of the tensors with `n` contravariant indices sending the basis tensor
with components `d` to `T d`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def ofComponents (T : (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B) :
    ℂT(fun _ : Fin n => Color.up) →ₗ[ℂ] B

declarations.name: Lorentz.ofComponents_coeffEquiv_symm
declarations.doc: `ofComponents T` contracts the coefficient tensor of its argument with `T`.
declarations.statement:
lemma ofComponents_coeffEquiv_symm (T : (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B)
    (c : (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ) :
    ofComponents T ((coeffEquiv n).symm c) = ∑ d, c d • T d

declarations.name: Lorentz.range_ofComponents
declarations.doc: The range of `ofComponents T` is the span of the vectors `T d`.
declarations.statement:
lemma range_ofComponents (T : (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B) :
    LinearMap.range (ofComponents T) = Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range T)

declarations.name: Lorentz.ofComponents_sum
declarations.doc: `ofComponents` of a sum of families is the sum of the maps.
declarations.statement:
lemma ofComponents_sum {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (T : ι → (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B) :
    ofComponents (fun d => ∑ i ∈ s, T i d) = ∑ i ∈ s, ofComponents (T i)

declarations.name: Lorentz.comp_ofComponents
declarations.doc:
A linear map applied after `ofComponents T` is `ofComponents` of its values on the
components.
declarations.statement:
lemma comp_ofComponents {B' : Type*} [AddCommGroup B'] [Module ℂ B'] (σ : B →ₗ[ℂ] B')
    (T : (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B) :
    σ ∘ₗ ofComponents T = ofComponents fun d => σ (T d)

declarations.name: Lorentz.ofComponents_comp_permT
declarations.doc:
Precomposing `ofComponents T` with the slot permutation `permT σ` reads the family at the
permuted index vectors `d ∘ σ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma ofComponents_comp_permT (σ : Fin n → Fin n)
    (h : IsReindexing (fun _ : Fin n => Color.up) (fun _ => Color.up) σ)
    (T : (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B) :
    ofComponents T ∘ₗ permT σ h = ofComponents fun d => T (d ∘ σ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.ofComponents_comp_permT_eq_neg
declarations.doc:
A family antisymmetric under reading its index vectors through `σ` gives a map
antisymmetric under `permT σ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma ofComponents_comp_permT_eq_neg (σ : Fin n → Fin n)
    (h : IsReindexing (fun _ : Fin n => Color.up) (fun _ => Color.up) σ)
    {T : (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B} (hT : ∀ d, T (d ∘ σ) = -T d) :
    ofComponents T ∘ₗ permT σ h = -ofComponents T

declarations.name: Lorentz.ofComponents_comp_permT_eq_self
declarations.doc:
A family symmetric under reading its index vectors through `σ` gives a map invariant under
`permT σ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma ofComponents_comp_permT_eq_self (σ : Fin n → Fin n)
    (h : IsReindexing (fun _ : Fin n => Color.up) (fun _ => Color.up) σ)
    {T : (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B} (hT : ∀ d, T (d ∘ σ) = T d) :
    ofComponents T ∘ₗ permT σ h = ofComponents T

declarations.name: Lorentz.isLorentzCovariant_ofComponents_iff
declarations.doc:
The map of a family is equivariant exactly when the family obeys the transformation law of
the components of a tensor with `n` four-vector indices.
declarations.statement:
lemma isLorentzCovariant_ofComponents_iff {repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) B}
    (T : (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B) :
    IsLorentzCovariant n B repLorentz (ofComponents T) ↔
      ∀ (g : SL(2,ℂ)) l, repLorentz g (T l) = ∑ a : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3,
        (∏ i, (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup g).1 (a i) (l i) : ℝ) : ℂ)) • T a

modules.title: Lorentz invariants of a rank-four tensor
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A rank-four tensor `T^{μνρσ}` has `4 ^ 4 = 256` components, and four invariant tensors can be
contracted with it:

* `η_{μν} η_{ρσ}`, `η_{μρ} η_{νσ}` and `η_{μσ} η_{νρ}`, the three pairings of the metric,
* `ε_{μνρσ}`, the Levi-Civita symbol.

These are the tensors `contractionTensor i`. There are no others: for an equivariant map
`f : ℂT(fun _ : Fin 4 => .up) →ₗ[ℂ] B`, `IsLorentzCovariant 4`, a vector of `LinearMap.range f ⊔ S`,
for `S` a Lorentz-stable submodule, is invariant exactly when it is a combination of the four
images `f (contractionTensor i)` plus an invariant of `S`, `mem_range_sup_invariant_iff` (H), and
`reducesInvariantsTo_span_contractionTensor` reads the left-to-right direction as a reduction.
The fourth tensor is a pseudoscalar, so it would drop out if reflections were allowed;
independence is not proved, and for a given `f` the four images may be dependent or zero.
When `f` is antisymmetric under exchanging its last two slots, two images already span: that
of `η_{μρ} η_{νσ}` and that of `ε_{μνρσ}` (B.4). When `f` is moreover symmetric under exchanging
its first two slots, both of those vanish too (B.5).

The four tensors are invariant, by `Λ η Λᵀ = η` and `det Λ = 1` (B); an invariant of the range of
`f` is the image of an invariant tensor, whose coefficient tensor is invariant (C); and such a
coefficient tensor is a combination of the four, two rotations cutting `256` coefficients to `22`
(D), a boost keeping only what it does not rescale (E), and the `22 × 22` integer equation left
being solved by one checked matrix identity (F, G).

## ii. Key results

- `Lorentz.RankFour.contractionTensor` : the four invariant tensors.
- `Lorentz.RankFour.exists_eq_sum` : an invariant coefficient tensor is a combination of them.
- `Lorentz.RankFour.mem_range_sup_invariant_iff` : the classification of the invariants.
- `Lorentz.RankFour.reducesInvariantsTo_span_contractionTensor` : the same as a reduction.
- `Lorentz.RankFour.span_range_contractionTensor_of_antisymm` : for a map antisymmetric in its
  last two slots, two of the four images span.
- `Lorentz.RankFour.apply_contractionTensor_one_of_symm_of_antisymm`,
  `Lorentz.RankFour.apply_contractionTensor_three_of_symm` : symmetry in the first two slots
  kills those two images.

- C. The metric, the Levi-Civita symbol and the invariant tensors

sections.text:
## A. Coefficient tensors

A direction is an element of `Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3`, time or one of the three axes; an index vector
`d : Fin 4 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3` puts one in each slot, and a coefficient tensor `c` assigns a
number to each. The components of a tensor, relabelled this way, are its coefficient tensor,
`coeffEquiv 4`, on which `g` acts by

`(act Λ c) a = ∑_d c_d Λ_{a₀ d₀} ⋯ Λ_{a₃ d₃}`,

with `a` free and `d` summed (`coeffEquiv_smul`), and a tensor is invariant exactly when its
coefficient tensor is `IsInvariantCoeff` (`invariant_iff_isInvariantCoeff`). Everything in this
paragraph is stated for any number of slots in `Invariants.Basic` and
`Invariants.LorentzCovariance` and used here at four.

## B. The four invariant tensors

## C. The metric, the Levi-Civita symbol and the invariant tensors

The metric is `minkowskiMatrixZ`, the integer form of `minkowskiMatrix`, and the symbol is
`leviCivitaSymbol`, read on an index vector through `finSumFinEquiv`. Both are integer valued
because sections F and G evaluate them in the kernel, which cannot compute with real numbers.
The metric pairings use the slots `(0,1)(2,3)`, `(0,2)(1,3)` and `(0,3)(1,2)`;
`contractionCoeff` holds the four coefficient tensors and `contractionTensor` the four tensors
with those coefficients, in that order.

## D. The four coefficient tensors are invariant

`Λ η Λᵀ = η` defines the Lorentz group; entry by entry it is
`LorentzGroup.sum_minkowskiMatrixZ_mul`, and a pair of metrics is two copies of it, one per
pair of slots (`act_outerPair`). The inner and split pairings are the outer one with the slots
permuted (`act_outerPair_comp`). The symbol against
four rows of `M` gives `det M` times the symbol of those rows (`sum_leviCivitaSymbol_mul_prod`),
and `det Λ = 1` here: the only use of the determinant, and the reason there are four invariants
and not three, a reflection having `det = -1`. `sum_pi_four` is bookkeeping.
## E. The four tensors are Lorentz invariant

## F. Exchanging the last two slots

Exchanging the slots `2` and `3`, `permT (Equiv.swap 2 3)`, fixes `η_{μν} η_{ρσ}`, the metric
being symmetric, and exchanges `η_{μρ} η_{νσ}` with `η_{μσ} η_{νρ}`. So a linear map `f` out of
the tensors with `f ∘ₗ permT (Equiv.swap 2 3) = -f` sends the first tensor to zero and the
third to minus the second, and the four images span what the second and the Levi-Civita image
span. Neither equivariance of `f` nor any structure on `B` beyond a complex module is used; the
two remaining images may still be dependent or zero.

## G. Exchanging the first two slots

Exchanging the slots `0` and `1`, `permT (Equiv.swap 0 1)`, exchanges `η_{μρ} η_{νσ}` with
`η_{μσ} η_{νρ}` and negates `ε_{μνρσ}`. So a linear map `f` out of the tensors with
`f ∘ₗ permT (Equiv.swap 0 1) = f` sends `ε_{μνρσ}` to zero, and if `f` is also antisymmetric in
its last two slots it sends `η_{μρ} η_{νσ}` to zero as well: in both a symmetric pair of slots
is contracted against an antisymmetric one. As in B.4 nothing beyond a complex module is used.

## H. Invariants of the range come from invariant coefficient tensors

An invariant of the range of `f` is the image of an invariant tensor
(`TensorSpecies.IsEquivariant.exists_invariant_add_of_mem_sup`): the adjoint of the action of
`g` on the coefficients is the action of `g†`. The coefficient tensor of an invariant tensor is
invariant, so what remains is to classify the invariant coefficient tensors, sections D to G.

## I. The rotations by `π` about the axes and the rotation `x → y → z → x`

The rotation by `π` about the `k`-th axis is `SL2C.halfTurn k`, with diagonal Lorentz matrix
fixing time and that axis and negating the other two, so it multiplies `c d` by `-1` once per
slot of `d` holding a negated direction (`act_halfTurn`), and where that sign is `-1`
invariance forces `c d = 0`. Call `d` half-turn fixed when all three signs are `1`
(`IsHalfTurnFixed`): with `n_t, n_x, n_y, n_z` the counts of each direction that says all four
have the same parity, so `xxyy` and `txyz` survive, `tttx` does not, and `64` of `256` remain.

The rotation `x → y → z → x` fixes time (`rotationCycle`) and permutes rather than rescales, so
the new coefficient at `a` is the old one at `cycIdx (cycIdx a)` (`act_rotationCycle`) and
invariance reads `c (cycIdx d) = c d`: `c` is constant on the orbit
`{d, cycIdx d, cycIdx (cycIdx d)}`, of three members unless `d` is `tttt`. Both actions are
stated for any number of slots in `Invariants.Basic`.

## J. The boost along an axis

## K. An invariant tensor has boost weight zero

The boosts along the axis `i` are `SL2C.boostAxis i t ht`, of rapidity `2 log t` for `t > 0`.
In each slot replace the coordinate directions by the light-cone directions `D₀ - Dᵢ`,
`D₀ + Dᵢ` and the two transverse ones: they are eigenvectors of the boost with eigenvalues
`t²`, `t⁻²`, `1`, `1` (`sum_boostAxis_lightConeCoeff`, imported), so their weights, the
exponents of `t`, are `2`, `-2`, `0`, `0` (`lightConeWeight`). A multi-index `κ` picks one per
slot and `lightConeComponent i c κ` contracts `c` against that choice; the boost scales it by
`t` to the total weight of `κ`, so `t = 2` kills every component of nonzero weight. Only the
`z`-axis is used below, and nothing claims these elements generate the group: F and G show that
what they force is enough.

## L. The weight-zero projection

Writing each coordinate direction in the light-cone basis recovers `c` from its light-cone
components (`eq_sum_lightConeComponent`), and for an invariant `c` only weight zero survives.
The projection that keeps total weight `m` is `Invariants.transitionZ`, built a slot at a time
and stated at any number of slots in `Invariants.LightCone`; each slot carries the factor `2`
of `lightConeCoeffInvZ`, so at four slots the projection is `2 ^ 4 = 16` times the true one.
That is the only place the `16` comes from.

## M. The `22` orbit coordinates and the orbit matrix

## N. The orbits

Write an index vector as a word, `tttt` or `txxt`. Cycling the axes carries one to another and
three cyclings return it, so they fall into orbits of at most three: `txxt`, `tyyt`, `tzzt`
form one, and `tttt` is alone. By D an invariant tensor vanishes off the `64` half-turn fixed
vectors and is constant on each orbit, and those `64` make `22` orbits, `21` of size three plus
`tttt`; `orbitRep` lists one from each, and the two lemmas below check at all `256` index
vectors that these cover the half-turn fixed ones without overlapping. So an invariant tensor is its
`22` values at the representatives, its orbit coordinates, which `ofOrbitCoord` inverts.

## O. The orbit matrix

Take `16 c_d = ∑_e transitionZ 2 d e 0 * c_e` at a representative and its two cyclings and add.
The left gives `48` times one orbit coordinate, the right collects the `256` index vectors into
the `22` orbits, and what is left is `M b = 48 b` with `M = orbitMatrix` below and
`48 = 3 * 16`. Entry `M k l` sums the transitions from the three cyclings of the representative
of orbit `k` into orbit `l` (`orbitMatrix_apply`, checked over `484` entries), so the printed
integers are not meant to be read; `M` is not symmetric, a row carrying three cyclings and a
column an orbit.

## P. The certificate

F leaves `M b = 48 b` for the orbit coordinates `b k = c (orbitRep k)`. Four solutions are
known, the orbit coordinates `v i = contractionOrbit i` of the tensors of B; there are no
others, by one identity between `22 × 22` integer matrices:

`M (M - 32) (M - 16) (M² - 44 M + 192) = 393216 • projector`,

where `projector = ∑ i, (v i) (w i)ᵀ` is four rank-one matrices built from the columns `v i`
and rows `w i = contractionWeight i`, so it sends any vector to a combination of the `v i`.
Lean checks it by computing all `484` entries of each side. On a solution `b` every factor
turns `M` into `48`, giving `48² - 44 * 48 + 192 = 384`, then `32`, `16`, `48`, so the left
sends `b` to `48 * 16 * 32 * 384 = 9437184` times `b` and the right to `393216 • (projector b)`.
As `9437184 = 393216 * 24` this leaves `projector b = 24 b` (`projector_mulVec`), writing `b`,
and with it `c`, as a combination of the four; the `24` is
`contractionWeight_mul_contractionOrbit`. The identity is
`λ (3λ - 2) (3λ - 1) (12λ² - 11λ + 1) / 4` at `λ = M / 48` with denominators cleared, but that
is only where it came from: the file proves nothing about the spectrum.

## Q. The classification of the invariants of an equivariant map

C to G reduce the invariants of `LinearMap.range f ⊔ S` to the span of the four images
`f (contractionTensor i)`; conversely those images are invariant, so a combination of them plus
an invariant of `S` is an invariant of `LinearMap.range f ⊔ S`.

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.contractionCoeff
declarations.doc: The four coefficient tensors: the three metric pairings, then the Levi-Civita symbol.
declarations.statement: def contractionCoeff : Fin 4 → (Fin 4 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℤ

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.contractionTensor
declarations.doc:
The four invariant tensors with four contravariant indices: `η_{μν} η_{ρσ}`,
`η_{μρ} η_{νσ}`, `η_{μσ} η_{νρ}` and `ε_{μνρσ}`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def contractionTensor (i : Fin 4) : ℂT(fun _ : Fin 4 => Color.up)

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.ofComponents_contractionTensor
declarations.doc:
`ofComponents T` sends each invariant tensor to the contraction of `T` with its
coefficients.
declarations.statement:
lemma ofComponents_contractionTensor (T : (Fin 4 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B) (i : Fin 4) :
    ofComponents T (contractionTensor i) = ∑ d, ((contractionCoeff i d : ℤ) : ℂ) • T d

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.sum_pi_four
declarations.doc: Bookkeeping: a sum over index vectors is a fourfold sum over directions.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_pi_four {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] (F : (Fin 4 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M) :
    ∑ d : Fin 4 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, F d
      = ∑ x : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, ∑ y : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, ∑ z : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3,
        ∑ w : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, F ![x, y, z, w]

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.act_outerPair
declarations.doc:
The pairing of slots `(0,1)` and `(2,3)` is fixed: two copies of
`LorentzGroup.sum_minkowskiMatrixZ_mul`.
declarations.statement:
lemma act_outerPair (Λ : LorentzGroup 3) (a : Fin 4 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    act Λ.1 (fun d => ((minkowskiMatrixZ (d 0) (d 1) * minkowskiMatrixZ (d 2) (d 3) : ℤ) : ℂ)) a
      = ((minkowskiMatrixZ (a 0) (a 1) * minkowskiMatrixZ (a 2) (a 3) : ℤ) : ℂ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.act_outerPair_comp
declarations.doc: The same for the slots permuted by `σ`, by renaming the summation variable.
declarations.statement:
lemma act_outerPair_comp (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin 4)) (Λ : LorentzGroup 3)
    (a : Fin 4 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    act Λ.1 (fun d => ((minkowskiMatrixZ (d (σ 0)) (d (σ 1))
        * minkowskiMatrixZ (d (σ 2)) (d (σ 3)) : ℤ) : ℂ)) a
      = ((minkowskiMatrixZ (a (σ 0)) (a (σ 1))
        * minkowskiMatrixZ (a (σ 2)) (a (σ 3)) : ℤ) : ℂ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.act_leviCivitaSymbol
declarations.doc:
The symbol is fixed by a Lorentz matrix of determinant `1`; in general it picks up `det Λ`,
by `sum_leviCivitaSymbol_mul_prod`.
declarations.statement:
lemma act_leviCivitaSymbol (Λ : LorentzGroup 3) (hΛ : Λ.1.det = 1) (a : Fin 4 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    act Λ.1 (fun d => ((leviCivitaSymbol fun μ => d (finSumFinEquiv μ) : ℤ) : ℂ)) a
      = ((leviCivitaSymbol fun μ => a (finSumFinEquiv μ) : ℤ) : ℂ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.isInvariantCoeff_contractionCoeff
declarations.doc: The four coefficient tensors are invariant.
declarations.statement:
lemma isInvariantCoeff_contractionCoeff (i : Fin 4) :
    IsInvariantCoeff fun d => ((contractionCoeff i d : ℤ) : ℂ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.contractionTensor_invariant
declarations.doc: Each of the four tensors is Lorentz invariant, its coefficient tensor being invariant.
declarations.statement:
lemma contractionTensor_invariant (i : Fin 4) (g : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    g • contractionTensor i = contractionTensor i

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.isReindexing_swap_two_three
declarations.doc: Exchanging the last two of four contravariant slots is a reindexing.
declarations.statement:
lemma isReindexing_swap_two_three :
    Tensor.IsReindexing (fun _ : Fin 4 => Color.up) (fun _ => Color.up)
      ⇑(Equiv.swap (2 : Fin 4) 3)

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.permT_swap_two_three_contractionTensor_zero
declarations.doc: `η_{μν} η_{ρσ}` is unchanged by exchanging its last two slots.
declarations.statement:
lemma permT_swap_two_three_contractionTensor_zero :
    Tensor.permT _ isReindexing_swap_two_three (contractionTensor 0) = contractionTensor 0

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.permT_swap_two_three_contractionTensor_one
declarations.doc: Exchanging the last two slots of `η_{μρ} η_{νσ}` gives `η_{μσ} η_{νρ}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma permT_swap_two_three_contractionTensor_one :
    Tensor.permT _ isReindexing_swap_two_three (contractionTensor 1) = contractionTensor 2

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.apply_contractionTensor_zero_of_antisymm
declarations.doc: A map antisymmetric in the last two slots sends `η_{μν} η_{ρσ}` to zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_contractionTensor_zero_of_antisymm
    (hf : f ∘ₗ Tensor.permT _ isReindexing_swap_two_three = -f) :
    f (contractionTensor 0) = 0

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.apply_contractionTensor_two_of_antisymm
declarations.doc:
A map antisymmetric in the last two slots sends `η_{μσ} η_{νρ}` to minus the image of
`η_{μρ} η_{νσ}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_contractionTensor_two_of_antisymm
    (hf : f ∘ₗ Tensor.permT _ isReindexing_swap_two_three = -f) :
    f (contractionTensor 2) = -f (contractionTensor 1)

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.span_range_contractionTensor_of_antisymm
declarations.doc:
For a map antisymmetric in the last two slots, the images of the four invariant tensors
span the same as the images of `η_{μρ} η_{νσ}` and `ε_{μνρσ}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma span_range_contractionTensor_of_antisymm
    (hf : f ∘ₗ Tensor.permT _ isReindexing_swap_two_three = -f) :
    Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range fun i => f (contractionTensor i))
      = Submodule.span ℂ {f (contractionTensor 1), f (contractionTensor 3)}

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.isReindexing_swap_zero_one
declarations.doc: Exchanging the first two of four contravariant slots is a reindexing.
declarations.statement:
lemma isReindexing_swap_zero_one :
    Tensor.IsReindexing (fun _ : Fin 4 => Color.up) (fun _ => Color.up)
      ⇑(Equiv.swap (0 : Fin 4) 1)

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.permT_swap_zero_one_contractionTensor_one
declarations.doc: Exchanging the first two slots of `η_{μρ} η_{νσ}` gives `η_{μσ} η_{νρ}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma permT_swap_zero_one_contractionTensor_one :
    Tensor.permT _ isReindexing_swap_zero_one (contractionTensor 1) = contractionTensor 2

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.permT_swap_zero_one_contractionTensor_three
declarations.doc: Exchanging the first two slots negates `ε_{μνρσ}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma permT_swap_zero_one_contractionTensor_three :
    Tensor.permT _ isReindexing_swap_zero_one (contractionTensor 3) = -contractionTensor 3

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.apply_contractionTensor_one_of_symm_of_antisymm
declarations.doc:
A map symmetric in the first two slots and antisymmetric in the last two sends
`η_{μρ} η_{νσ}` to zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_contractionTensor_one_of_symm_of_antisymm
    (hs : f ∘ₗ Tensor.permT _ isReindexing_swap_zero_one = f)
    (ha : f ∘ₗ Tensor.permT _ isReindexing_swap_two_three = -f) :
    f (contractionTensor 1) = 0

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.apply_contractionTensor_three_of_symm
declarations.doc: A map symmetric in the first two slots sends `ε_{μνρσ}` to zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_contractionTensor_three_of_symm
    (hs : f ∘ₗ Tensor.permT _ isReindexing_swap_zero_one = f) :
    f (contractionTensor 3) = 0

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.IsHalfTurnFixed
declarations.doc:
All three half turns fix the coefficient at `d`, that is the sign product is `1` for each
axis. Equivalently, and not used below, all four directions occur an even number of times
among the slots, or all four an odd number.
declarations.statement: def IsHalfTurnFixed (d : Fin 4 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : Prop
instance : DecidablePred IsHalfTurnFixed

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.eq_zero_of_not_isHalfTurnFixed
declarations.doc: An invariant coefficient tensor vanishes off the half-turn fixed index vectors.

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.sixteen_mul_eq_sum_transitionZ
declarations.doc: An invariant coefficient tensor is its own weight-zero projection.

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.orbitRep
declarations.doc: One index vector from each of the `22` orbits, checked by the two lemmas below.
declarations.statement: def orbitRep : Fin 22 → Fin 4 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.orbit
declarations.doc: The `k`-th representative and its two cyclings; for `tttt` the three coincide.
declarations.statement: def orbit (k : Fin 22) : Finset (Fin 4 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.isHalfTurnFixed_iff_exists_mem_orbit
declarations.doc: The vectors in one of the `22` orbits are exactly the half-turn fixed ones, a finite check.
declarations.statement:
lemma isHalfTurnFixed_iff_exists_mem_orbit :
    ∀ d, IsHalfTurnFixed d ↔ ∃ k, d ∈ orbit k

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.disjoint_orbit
declarations.doc: Different orbits share no index vector, a finite check.
declarations.statement: lemma disjoint_orbit : ∀ k l : Fin 22, k ≠ l → Disjoint (orbit k) (orbit l)

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.eq_of_mem_orbit
declarations.doc: An index vector lies in at most one orbit.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_of_mem_orbit {k l : Fin 22} {d : Fin 4 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3}
    (hk : d ∈ orbit k) (hl : d ∈ orbit l) : k = l

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.eq_orbitRep_of_mem_orbit
declarations.doc: A tensor unchanged by cycling takes, on an orbit, its value at the representative.

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.ofOrbitCoord
declarations.doc: The coefficient tensor with orbit coordinates `b`, and `0` off the orbits.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def ofOrbitCoord (b : Fin 22 → ℂ) (d : Fin 4 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : ℂ

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.eq_ofOrbitCoord
declarations.doc: An invariant coefficient tensor is rebuilt from its `22` orbit coordinates.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_ofOrbitCoord {c : (Fin 4 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ} (hc : IsInvariantCoeff c) :
    c = ofOrbitCoord fun k => c (orbitRep k)

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.sum_mul_ofOrbitCoord
declarations.doc: Contracting against such a tensor collects the `256` index vectors into the `22` orbits.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_mul_ofOrbitCoord (f : (Fin 4 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ) (b : Fin 22 → ℂ) :
    ∑ e, f e * ofOrbitCoord b e = ∑ l, (∑ e ∈ orbit l, f e) * b l

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.orbitMatrix
declarations.doc:
Forty-eight times the weight-zero projection along `z` on the orbit coordinates, the three
cyclings summed and not averaged, so `48 = 3 * 16`. Meaningful only through
`orbitMatrix_apply`.
declarations.statement: def orbitMatrix : Matrix (Fin 22) (Fin 22) ℤ

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.orbitMatrix_apply
declarations.doc: Each entry sums the `z`-axis transitions from orbit `k` into orbit `l`, a finite check.
declarations.statement:
lemma orbitMatrix_apply : ∀ k l : Fin 22,
    orbitMatrix k l = ∑ e ∈ orbit l, (transitionZ 2 (orbitRep k) e 0
      + transitionZ 2 (cycIdx (orbitRep k)) e 0
      + transitionZ 2 (cycIdx (cycIdx (orbitRep k))) e 0)

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.orbitMatrix_mulVec
declarations.doc: The orbit coordinates of an invariant coefficient tensor satisfy `M b = 48 b`.
declarations.statement:
lemma orbitMatrix_mulVec {c : (Fin 4 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ}
    (hc : IsInvariantCoeff c) :
    orbitMatrix.map (Int.cast : ℤ → ℂ) *ᵥ (fun k => c (orbitRep k))
      = (48 : ℂ) • fun k => c (orbitRep k)

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.contractionOrbit
declarations.doc: The orbit coordinates of the `i`-th coefficient tensor.
declarations.statement: def contractionOrbit (i : Fin 4) (k : Fin 22) : ℤ

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.contractionWeight
declarations.doc:
Four rows of `22` integers paired with `contractionOrbit` to build `projector`. Found by
computation and characterised by `contractionWeight_mul_contractionOrbit`; unrelated to boost
weight.
declarations.statement: def contractionWeight : Fin 4 → Fin 22 → ℤ

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.contractionWeight_mul_contractionOrbit
declarations.doc: The weight rows and orbit coordinates pair to `24 δᵢⱼ`, a finite check.
declarations.statement:
lemma contractionWeight_mul_contractionOrbit : ∀ i j : Fin 4,
    ∑ k, contractionWeight i k * contractionOrbit j k = if i = j then 24 else 0

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.projector
declarations.doc: Four rank-one matrices, so it sends any vector to a combination of the `v i`.
declarations.statement: def projector : Matrix (Fin 22) (Fin 22) ℤ

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.certificate
declarations.doc: An identity between `22 × 22` integer matrices, a finite check over `484` entries.
declarations.statement:
lemma certificate :
    orbitMatrix * (orbitMatrix - 32 • 1) * (orbitMatrix - 16 • 1)
      * (orbitMatrix * orbitMatrix - 44 • orbitMatrix + 192 • 1) = 393216 • projector

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.projector_mulVec
declarations.doc:
The integer projector matrix acts on invariant orbit coordinates by multiplication by `24`.
The `24` is the normalization of `projector`: each factor of the certificate acts on such a
vector as a scalar, `M` by `48`, `M - z` by `48 - z` and the quadratic factor by
`48 ^ 2 - 44 * 48 + 192 = 384`, so the left-hand side scales it by
`48 * 32 * 16 * 384 = 9437184`, and dividing by the `393216` on the right leaves `24`.
declarations.statement:
lemma projector_mulVec {c : (Fin 4 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ} (hc : IsInvariantCoeff c) :
    projector.map (Int.cast : ℤ → ℂ) *ᵥ (fun k => c (orbitRep k))
      = (24 : ℂ) • fun k => c (orbitRep k)

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.orbitCoord_eq
declarations.doc:
`24` times an orbit coordinate of an invariant tensor, read entry by entry off the previous
lemma: `projector` is built from the columns `contractionOrbit i` and the rows
`contractionWeight i`.
declarations.statement:
lemma orbitCoord_eq {c : (Fin 4 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ} (hc : IsInvariantCoeff c)
    (k : Fin 22) :
    24 * c (orbitRep k)
      = ∑ i, (contractionOrbit i k : ℂ) * ∑ l, (contractionWeight i l : ℂ) * c (orbitRep l)

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.exists_eq_sum
declarations.doc: An invariant coefficient tensor is a combination of the four.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_eq_sum {c : (Fin 4 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ} (hc : IsInvariantCoeff c) :
    ∃ a : Fin 4 → ℂ, c = fun d => ∑ i, a i * ((contractionCoeff i d : ℤ) : ℂ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.reducesInvariantsTo_span_contractionTensor
declarations.doc:
The invariants of the range of `f` reduce to the span of the images of the four invariant
tensors.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_span_contractionTensor (hf : IsLorentzCovariant 4 B repLorentz f) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (fun g : SL(2,ℂ) => repLorentz g) (LinearMap.range f)
      (Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range fun i => f (contractionTensor i)))

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.mem_range_sup_invariant_iff
declarations.doc:
A vector of `LinearMap.range f ⊔ S`, for `S` a Lorentz-stable submodule, is invariant exactly
when it is a combination of the images of the four invariant tensors plus an invariant of
`S`. `hS` is used only left to right.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_range_sup_invariant_iff (hf : IsLorentzCovariant 4 B repLorentz f) (x : B)
    (S : Submodule ℂ B) (hS : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) :
    (x ∈ LinearMap.range f ⊔ S ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x)
      ↔ ∃ a : Fin 4 → ℂ, ∃ y ∈ S, x = ∑ i, a i • f (contractionTensor i) + y
        ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g y = y

modules.title: Lorentz invariants of a single four-vector index
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A four-vector `T^{μ}` has no Lorentz invariant but `0`. There is nothing to contract it with:
the metric takes two indices and the Levi-Civita symbol four. For an equivariant map
`f : ℂT(fun _ : Fin 1 => .up) →ₗ[ℂ] B`, `IsLorentzCovariant 1`, that is `eq_zero_of_invariant`,
and `reducesInvariantsTo_bot`, the form the Standard Model files use, is the same statement
modulo a Lorentz-stable submodule `S`.

The invariants of the range of `f` are the images of invariant tensors, so it is enough that an
invariant coefficient tensor `c` (`Invariants.Basic`) vanishes. Along a spatial axis the four
light-cone directions carry boost weights `2`, `-2`, `0`, `0`, and an invariant `c` has no
light-cone component of nonzero weight, which with one index says `c_d = 0` unless `d` is one of
the two directions transverse to time and to that axis (A). No direction is transverse to all three
axes, so running the three axes in turn leaves `c = 0` (B). Section C applies this to `f`.

## ii. Key results

- `eq_zero_of_invariant` : every Lorentz invariant in the range of `f` is zero: one index carry no
  invariant contraction
- `reducesInvariantsTo_bot` : the range of `f` reduces to `⊥`: a Lorentz invariant of
  `LinearMap.range f ⊔ S`, for `S` a Lorentz-stable submodule, lies in `S`

## iii. Table of contents

- A. What one axis leaves
- B. The classification of the Lorentz invariants
- C. The invariants of an equivariant map

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. What one axis leaves

The boost along the axis `i` scales the light-cone directions `D₀ - Dᵢ`, `D₀ + Dᵢ` and the two
transverse ones by `t²`, `t⁻²`, `1`, `1`, so their weights are `2`, `-2`, `0`, `0`. An invariant
`c` has no light-cone component of nonzero weight, so writing `c_d` in the light-cone basis
leaves only the two weight-zero directions, and their coefficients in `d` vanish unless `d` is
itself transverse.

## B. The classification of the Lorentz invariants

No direction is transverse to all three axes at once, so applying A to the three axes in turn
leaves no coefficient standing.

## C. The invariants of an equivariant map

The invariants of the range of an equivariant map come from invariant tensors, whose coefficient
tensors are invariant, so section B leaves none of them.

modules.title: Lorentz invariants of three four-vector indices
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A rank-three tensor `T^{μνρ}` has no Lorentz invariant but `0`. Nothing ties three indices:
the metric takes two and the Levi-Civita symbol four, and an odd number is left over either way.
For an equivariant map `f : ℂT(fun _ : Fin 3 => .up) →ₗ[ℂ] B`, `IsLorentzCovariant 3`, that is
`eq_zero_of_invariant`, and `reducesInvariantsTo_bot`, the form the Standard Model files use, is
the same statement modulo a Lorentz-stable submodule `S`.

The invariants of the range of `f` are the images of invariant tensors, so it is enough that an
invariant coefficient tensor `c` (`Invariants.Basic`) vanishes. One axis then does all the work,
with a parity argument in place of a certificate. Along a spatial axis the four light-cone
directions carry boost weights `2`, `-2`, `0`, `0`, and an invariant `c` has no light-cone component
of nonzero weight. In a multi-index of total weight `0` the `+2` and `-2` slots pair off, leaving an
odd number of the three slots transverse. The half turn about the axis, the rotation by `π`, fixes
time and the axis and negates the two transverse directions (A), so it multiplies each weight-zero
component by `-1` to an odd power, that is by `-1`, and an invariant component both fixed and
negated is `0` (B). Every light-cone component of `c` vanishes, so `c` does, and with it the
invariant. Section C applies this to `f`.

## ii. Key results

- `eq_zero_of_invariant` : every Lorentz invariant in the range of `f` is zero: three indices carry
  no invariant contraction
- `reducesInvariantsTo_bot` : the range of `f` reduces to `⊥`: a Lorentz invariant of
  `LinearMap.range f ⊔ S`, for `S` a Lorentz-stable submodule, lies in `S`

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The half turn about a spatial axis
- B. The classification of the Lorentz invariants
- C. The invariants of an equivariant map

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The half turn about a spatial axis

The half turn about the axis `i` is the rotation by `π` about it, `SL2C.halfTurn i` from
`SL2C.AxisRotations`. Its Lorentz matrix is diagonal, fixing time and the axis and negating
the two transverse directions, so on the light-cone directions of that axis it is `1` on the
two of weight `±2` and `-1` on the two transverse ones (`lightConeSign`).

## B. The classification of the Lorentz invariants

Writing a coefficient tensor in the light-cone basis of one axis leaves only the multi-indices
of total weight zero, the others being killed by the boost. The half turn about that axis
negates exactly those, so they vanish too and nothing is left.

## C. The invariants of an equivariant map

The invariants of the range of an equivariant map come from invariant tensors, whose coefficient
tensors are invariant, so section B leaves none of them.

declarations.name: Lorentz.lightConeSign
declarations.doc:
The sign the half turn about an axis gives each light-cone direction of that axis: `1` on
the two of weight `±2`, `-1` on the two transverse ones.
declarations.statement: def lightConeSign (κ : Fin 4) : ℤ

declarations.name: Lorentz.sum_halfTurn_lightConeCoeff
declarations.doc:
The half turn about the axis `i` acts on each light-cone direction along that axis
by its sign.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_halfTurn_lightConeCoeff (i : Fin 3) (κ : Fin 4) (ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    ∑ μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, lightConeCoeff i κ μ *
        (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup (SL2C.halfTurn i)).1 ν μ : ℝ) : ℂ)
      = ((lightConeSign κ : ℤ) : ℂ) * lightConeCoeff i κ ν

declarations.name: Lorentz.sum_prod_halfTurn_lightConeCoeff
declarations.doc:
The scalar behind the action of the half turn on a light-cone multi-index: the half
turn acts slot by slot, so the product of the per-slot signs factors out.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_prod_halfTurn_lightConeCoeff (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → Fin 4)
    (a : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    ∑ d : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, (∏ j, lightConeCoeff i (c j) (d j)) *
        (∏ j, (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup (SL2C.halfTurn i)).1 (a j) (d j) : ℝ) : ℂ))
      = ((∏ j, lightConeSign (c j) : ℤ) : ℂ) * ∏ j, lightConeCoeff i (c j) (a j)

declarations.name: Lorentz.prod_lightConeSign_of_sum_lightConeWeight_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
A light-cone multi-index of three slots and total boost weight zero has an odd
number of transverse slots, so the half turn acts on it by `-1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma prod_lightConeSign_of_sum_lightConeWeight_eq_zero (c : Fin 3 → Fin 4)
    (hc : (∑ j, lightConeWeight (c j)) = 0) : ∏ j, lightConeSign (c j) = -1

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankThree.lightConeComponent_act_halfTurn
declarations.doc: The half turn multiplies a light-cone component by the product of the signs of its slots.
declarations.statement:
lemma lightConeComponent_act_halfTurn {n : ℕ} (i : Fin 3)
    (c : (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ) (κ : Fin n → Fin 4) :
    lightConeComponent i (act (SL2C.toLorentzGroup (SL2C.halfTurn i)).1 c) κ
      = ((∏ s, lightConeSign (κ s) : ℤ) : ℂ) * lightConeComponent i c κ

declarations.statement:
lemma eq_zero_of_isInvariantCoeff {c : (Fin 3 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ}

modules.title: Lorentz invariants among two four-vector indices
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A rank-two tensor `T^{μν}` has a single Lorentz invariant up to scale, its contraction with the
metric: nothing else ties two indices, the Levi-Civita symbol needing four. For an equivariant
map `f : ℂT(fun _ : Fin 2 => .up) →ₗ[ℂ] B`, `IsLorentzCovariant 2`, every Lorentz invariant in the
range of `f` is a multiple of `f metric`, the image of the metric `η` (A), and modulo a
Lorentz-stable submodule `S` the invariants of `LinearMap.range f ⊔ S` reduce to the line through
it (C). For a given `f` the image may be zero.

The invariants of the range of `f` are the images of invariant tensors, so it is enough that an
invariant coefficient tensor `c` (`Invariants.Basic`) is a multiple of the Minkowski metric, and
three kinds of transformation pin `c` down (B). The half turn about each axis has a diagonal
Lorentz matrix with entries `±1`, and for `μ ≠ ν` one of the three negates `c_{μν}`, so the
off-diagonal coefficients vanish. The cyclic rotation `x → y → z → x` permutes the spatial
directions, so `c_xx = c_yy = c_zz`. The boost along `z` scales the light-cone component of `c`
along `D₀ - D_z` in both slots by `t⁴`, so that component vanishes, and with the off-diagonal
coefficients gone it is `c_tt + c_zz`. So `c` is `c_tt` times the Minkowski metric.

## ii. Key results

- `Lorentz.RankTwo.metric` : the metric `η` with the colours of `IsLorentzCovariant 2`.
- `Lorentz.RankTwo.exists_smul_map_metric_of_invariant` : an invariant in the range of `f` is a
  multiple of `f metric`.
- `Lorentz.RankTwo.reducesInvariantsTo_span_metric` : the same modulo a stable submodule.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The metric
- B. The classification of the invariant coefficient tensors
- C. The invariants of an equivariant map

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The metric

## B. The classification of the invariant coefficient tensors

The half turns kill the off-diagonal coefficients, the cyclic rotation equates the three
spatial diagonal ones, and the boost along `z` relates the spatial diagonal to the time
diagonal. Together these leave `c_tt` times the metric.
## C. The invariants of an equivariant map

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankTwo.metric
declarations.doc:
The metric `η` on two contravariant indices, with its colours relabelled from
`![.up, .up]` to `fun _ => .up`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def metric : ℂT(fun _ : Fin 2 => Color.up)

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankTwo.metric_invariant
declarations.doc: The metric is Lorentz invariant.
declarations.statement: lemma metric_invariant (g : SL(2,ℂ)) : g • metric = metric

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankTwo.coeffEquiv_symm_minkowskiMatrixZ
declarations.doc: The coefficient tensor of the metric is the Minkowski metric.
declarations.statement:
lemma coeffEquiv_symm_minkowskiMatrixZ :
    (coeffEquiv 2).symm (fun d => ((minkowskiMatrixZ (d 0) (d 1) : ℤ) : ℂ)) = metric

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankTwo.ofComponents_metric
declarations.doc: `ofComponents T` sends the metric to the contraction `η_{μν} T^{μν}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma ofComponents_metric (T : (Fin 2 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B) :
    ofComponents T metric
      = ∑ d : Fin 2 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, ((minkowskiMatrixZ (d 0) (d 1) : ℤ) : ℂ) • T d

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankTwo.exists_halfTurnSign_mul_ne_one
declarations.doc:
Two distinct directions are told apart by the half turn about some axis: it keeps one and
negates the other, a finite check.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_halfTurnSign_mul_ne_one :
    ∀ μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, μ ≠ ν → ∃ k, halfTurnSign k μ * halfTurnSign k ν ≠ 1

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankTwo.eq_zero_of_ne
declarations.doc:
An invariant coefficient tensor has no off-diagonal coefficients: for `μ ≠ ν` some half
turn multiplies `c_{μν}` by `-1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_zero_of_ne {c : (Fin 2 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ} (hc : IsInvariantCoeff c)
    {d : Fin 2 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3} (hd : d 0 ≠ d 1) : c d = 0

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankTwo.apply_inr_inr_eq
declarations.doc:
The three spatial diagonal coefficients of an invariant coefficient tensor agree: the
cyclic rotation carries `c_xx` to `c_yy` to `c_zz`.
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_inr_inr_eq {c : (Fin 2 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ} (hc : IsInvariantCoeff c)
    (j : Fin 3) : c ![Sum.inr j, Sum.inr j] = c ![Sum.inr 2, Sum.inr 2]

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankTwo.apply_inl_inl_add_apply_inr_inr
declarations.doc:
The time and spatial diagonal coefficients of an invariant coefficient tensor are opposite.
The boost along `z` scales the light-cone component along `D₀ - D_z` in both slots by `t⁴`, so
that component, `c_tt - c_tz - c_zt + c_zz`, vanishes, and the mixed terms are `0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_inl_inl_add_apply_inr_inr {c : (Fin 2 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ}
    (hc : IsInvariantCoeff c) : c ![Sum.inl 0, Sum.inl 0] + c ![Sum.inr 2, Sum.inr 2] = 0

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankTwo.eq_smul_minkowskiMatrixZ
declarations.doc: An invariant coefficient tensor is `c_tt` times the Minkowski metric.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_smul_minkowskiMatrixZ {c : (Fin 2 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ} (hc : IsInvariantCoeff c)
    (d : Fin 2 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    c d = c ![Sum.inl 0, Sum.inl 0] * ((minkowskiMatrixZ (d 0) (d 1) : ℤ) : ℂ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankTwo.reducesInvariantsTo_span_metric
declarations.doc:
The invariants of the range of `f` reduce to the line through the image `f metric` of the
metric: a Lorentz invariant of `LinearMap.range f ⊔ S`, for `S` a Lorentz-stable submodule, is
a multiple of `f metric` plus an element of `S`.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_span_metric (hf : IsLorentzCovariant 2 B repLorentz f) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (fun g : SL(2,ℂ) => repLorentz g) (LinearMap.range f)
      (ℂ ∙ f metric)

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankTwo.exists_smul_map_metric_add_of_invariant
declarations.doc:
Every Lorentz invariant of `LinearMap.range f ⊔ S`, for `S` a Lorentz-stable submodule, is a
multiple of the image `f metric` of the metric plus an element of `S`.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_smul_map_metric_add_of_invariant (hf : IsLorentzCovariant 2 B repLorentz f)
    (S : Submodule ℂ B) (hS : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) {x : B}
    (hx : x ∈ LinearMap.range f ⊔ S) (hinv : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x) :
    ∃ a : ℂ, ∃ y ∈ S, x = a • f metric + y

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankTwo.exists_smul_map_metric_of_invariant
declarations.doc:
Every Lorentz invariant in the range of `f` is a multiple of the image `f metric` of the
metric.

modules.title: The Lorentz mixing of derivative slots
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A Lorentz transformation mixes each derivative slot of a symbol through a column `Λ_{b a}`
of the Lorentz matrix. On families indexed by multisets of directions this is the operator
`lorentzMix`: peel one direction `a`, put it back as every direction `b` weighted by
`Λ_{b a}`, and mix what is left; peeling commutes, so the operator descends to multisets,
and `lorentzMix_ofFn` is its tuple form. The correction terms of a covariant derivative are
Leibniz convolutions `derivConv` over the multiset antidiagonal, and `lorentzMix` is a
morphism for the convolution. The Lorentz law of any covariant tower built one slot at a
time from a covariant correction is then one induction, `repLorentz_tower`. Nothing here
depends on a gauge group.

## ii. Key results

- `Lorentz.lorentzMix`, `Lorentz.lorentzMix_ofFn` : the mixing operator and its tuple form.
- `Lorentz.derivConv`, `Lorentz.lorentzMix_derivConv` : the Leibniz convolution, and the
  mixing operator as a morphism for it.
- `Lorentz.repLorentz_tower` : the Lorentz law of an abstract covariant tower.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Lorentz mixing of derivative slots
- B. The Leibniz convolution
- C. The Lorentz law of a covariant tower

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The Lorentz mixing of derivative slots
## B. The Leibniz convolution

## C. The Lorentz law of a covariant tower

A covariant tower is built one slot at a time: the tower along `l 0 :: l'` is the tower
along `l'` with one more plain derivative, plus a correction `C (l 0)` applied to the tower
along `l'`. The induction is run once, for an abstract tower with a Lorentz covariant
correction that is linear in the family it corrects and lets a twist of the value index
through.

declarations.name: Lorentz.lorentzMixStep
declarations.doc:
One peeling step of the Lorentz mixing: the direction `a` is removed from the multiset
index of the family and put back as every direction `b`, weighted by `Λ_{b a}`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def lorentzMixStep (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (a : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (G : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M) : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M

declarations.doc: Peeling two directions commutes, so the mixing is well defined on a multiset.
declarations.statement: instance (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) : LeftCommutative (lorentzMixStep (M := M) Λ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.lorentzMix
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz mixing of a multiset-indexed family along a multiset `s` of directions:
every direction of `s` is peeled and replaced by all directions, weighted by the
corresponding column of the Lorentz matrix.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def lorentzMix (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (G : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M

declarations.name: Lorentz.lorentzMix_zero
declarations.statement: lemma lorentzMix_zero : lorentzMix Λ G 0 = G

declarations.name: Lorentz.lorentzMix_cons_apply
declarations.doc: Mixing along `a ::ₘ s` peels `a` after mixing along `s`.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzMix_cons_apply (a : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    lorentzMix Λ G (a ::ₘ s) t = ∑ b, L[Λ] b a • lorentzMix Λ G s (b ::ₘ t)

declarations.name: Lorentz.lorentzMix_apply_add
declarations.doc:
Evaluating a mixed family away from the empty multiset is mixing the translated
family at the empty multiset.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzMix_apply_add (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    ∀ (G : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M) (t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)),
      lorentzMix Λ G s t = lorentzMix Λ (fun r => G (r + t)) s 0

declarations.name: Lorentz.lorentzMix_cons_zero
declarations.doc: Peeling at the empty multiset: the peeled direction is pushed into the family.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzMix_cons_zero (a : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    lorentzMix Λ G (a ::ₘ s) 0 = ∑ b, L[Λ] b a • lorentzMix Λ (fun t => G (b ::ₘ t)) s 0

declarations.name: Lorentz.lorentzMix_map
declarations.doc: The mixing operator commutes with any linear map applied to the values.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzMix_map (Φ : M →ₗ[ℂ] N) (s t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    Φ (lorentzMix Λ G s t) = lorentzMix Λ (fun r => Φ (G r)) s t

declarations.name: Lorentz.lorentzMix_smul_fam
declarations.doc: The mixing operator is homogeneous in the family.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzMix_smul_fam (c : ℂ) (s t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    lorentzMix Λ (fun r => c • G r) s t = c • lorentzMix Λ G s t

declarations.name: Lorentz.lorentzMix_add_fam
declarations.doc: The mixing operator is additive in the family.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzMix_add_fam (G₁ G₂ : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M)
    (s t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    lorentzMix Λ (fun r => G₁ r + G₂ r) s t = lorentzMix Λ G₁ s t + lorentzMix Λ G₂ s t

declarations.name: Lorentz.lorentzMix_sum_fam
declarations.doc: The mixing operator commutes with finite sums of families.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzMix_sum_fam {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (H : ι → Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M)
    (s t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    lorentzMix Λ (fun r => ∑ i, H i r) s t = ∑ i, lorentzMix Λ (H i) s t

declarations.name: Lorentz.lorentzMix_ofFn
declarations.doc:
The mixing operator agrees with the tuple form of the Lorentz law: along an ordered
tuple of directions it is the sum over all tuples with one Lorentz matrix factor per
slot.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzMix_ofFn {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    lorentzMix Λ G (List.ofFn l) t =
      ∑ p : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3),
        (∏ i, L[Λ] (p i) (l i)) • G ((List.ofFn p : List (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) + t)

declarations.name: Lorentz.derivConv
declarations.doc:
The Leibniz convolution of two families of derivative symbols: the sum over the
splittings of the multiset of the products of the two symbols.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def derivConv (f g : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) : B

declarations.name: Lorentz.derivConv_cons
declarations.doc: One derivative peeled off a convolution lands on one factor or the other.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivConv_cons (f g : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B) (a : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    derivConv f g (a ::ₘ s) =
      derivConv f (fun r => g (a ::ₘ r)) s + derivConv (fun r => f (a ::ₘ r)) g s

declarations.name: Lorentz.derivConv_sum_right
declarations.doc: The convolution is linear in its right-hand family.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivConv_sum_right {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (f : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B)
    (c : ι → ℂ) (g : ι → Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    derivConv f (fun r => ∑ i, c i • g i r) s = ∑ i, c i • derivConv f (g i) s

declarations.name: Lorentz.derivConv_sum_left
declarations.doc: The convolution is linear in its left-hand family.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivConv_sum_left {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (g : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B)
    (c : ι → ℂ) (f : ι → Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    derivConv (fun r => ∑ i, c i • f i r) g s = ∑ i, c i • derivConv (f i) g s

declarations.name: Lorentz.lorentzMix_derivConv
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz mixing operator is a morphism for the Leibniz convolution: mixing the two
factors separately and convolving is the same as convolving and then mixing.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzMix_derivConv (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    ∀ (f g : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B),
      derivConv (fun x => lorentzMix Λ f x 0) (fun y => lorentzMix Λ g y 0) s =
        lorentzMix Λ (derivConv f g) s 0

declarations.name: Lorentz.repLorentz_derivConv
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz law of a Leibniz convolution: the mixing operator is a morphism for the
convolution, so a convolution of two families with Lorentz laws has one too.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_derivConv {repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) B}
    (hmul : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (b₁ b₂ : B),
      repLorentz Λ (b₁ * b₂) = repLorentz Λ b₁ * repLorentz Λ b₂)
    (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (f f' g g' : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B)
    (hf : ∀ x, repLorentz Λ (f x) = lorentzMix Λ f' x 0)
    (hg : ∀ y, repLorentz Λ (g y) = lorentzMix Λ g' y 0) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    repLorentz Λ (derivConv f g s) = lorentzMix Λ (derivConv f' g') s 0

declarations.name: Lorentz.repLorentz_tower
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz law of a covariant tower `T` built by the step `hstep` from a correction
`C`, transforming into a tower `T'` built by the same step: the seed of `T` transforms
into the seed of `T'` with the value index twisted by `τ` (`hzero`), and the correction is
Lorentz covariant (`hC`), linear in the family it corrects (`hClin`) and lets the twist
through (`hCτ`). Then the covariant slots mix by their own columns of the Lorentz matrix,
the plain slots by `lorentzMix`, and the value index by `τ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_tower {K : Type} [Field K] {W : Type} [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W]
    [Module K B] [SMulCommClass K ℂ B] (Λ : SL(2,ℂ))
    (T T' : (n : ℕ) → (Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) → Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → W →ₗ[K] B)
    (C : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → W →ₗ[K] B) →
      Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → W →ₗ[K] B)
    (τ : W →ₗ[K] W)
    (hstep : ∀ (n : ℕ) (l : Fin (n + 1) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)),
      T (n + 1) l s = T n (fun i => l i.succ) (l 0 ::ₘ s) + C (l 0) (T n fun i => l i.succ) s)
    (hstep' : ∀ (n : ℕ) (l : Fin (n + 1) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)),
      T' (n + 1) l s = T' n (fun i => l i.succ) (l 0 ::ₘ s) + C (l 0) (T' n fun i => l i.succ) s)
    (hzero : ∀ (l : Fin 0 → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : W),
      repLorentz Λ (T 0 l s φ) = lorentzMix Λ (fun t => T' 0 l t (τ φ)) s 0)
    (hC : ∀ (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (G G' : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → W →ₗ[K] B),
      (∀ y χ, repLorentz Λ (G y χ) = lorentzMix Λ (fun t => G' t χ) y 0) →
      ∀ (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : W), repLorentz Λ (C ρ G s φ) =
        ∑ a, L[Λ] a ρ • lorentzMix Λ (fun t => C a G' t φ) s 0)
    (hClin : ∀ (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] (c : ι → ℂ)
      (G : ι → Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → W →ₗ[K] B) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
      (φ : W), C ρ (fun t => ∑ i, c i • G i t) s φ = ∑ i, c i • C ρ (G i) s φ)
    (hCτ : ∀ (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (G : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → W →ₗ[K] B)
      (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : W),
      C ρ (fun t => G t ∘ₗ τ) s φ = C ρ G s (τ φ)) :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : W),
      repLorentz Λ (T n l s φ) =
        ∑ p : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3),
          (∏ i, L[Λ] (p i) (l i)) • lorentzMix Λ (fun t => T' n p t (τ φ)) s 0

modules.title: The Minkowski matrix over the integers
modules.doc:
The Minkowski matrix with integer entries, so that the kernel can evaluate it.

## i. Overview

The entries of `minkowskiMatrix` are integers, but it is a matrix over `ℝ`, and the kernel
cannot evaluate arithmetic in `ℝ`. Statements which a decision procedure has to evaluate are
therefore stated with `minkowskiMatrixZ`, the same diagonal matrix `diag(1, -1, …, -1)` taken
over `ℤ`. The bridge back is `minkowskiMatrixZ.cast_apply`, which casts an entry to the
corresponding entry of `minkowskiMatrix`; the remaining lemmas are the entry values and the
symmetry, matching the `minkowskiMatrix` API.

## ii. Key results

- `minkowskiMatrixZ` : the Minkowski matrix over `ℤ`.
- `minkowskiMatrixZ.cast_apply` : its cast to `ℝ` is `minkowskiMatrix`, entry by entry.
- `minkowskiMatrixZ.inl_0_inl_0`, `minkowskiMatrixZ.inr_i_inr_i`,
  `minkowskiMatrixZ.off_diag_zero` : the entries.
- `minkowskiMatrixZ.comm` : it is symmetric.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Minkowski matrix over the integers

## iv. References

The real Minkowski matrix and its API are in `Physlib.Relativity.MinkowskiMatrix`.

modules.title: Three anticommuting matrices are the most `2 × 2` can hold
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A family `τ` of `2 × 2` complex matrices is anticommuting when `τ_a τ_b + τ_b τ_a = 2 δ_ab 1`:
each `τ_a` squares to `1` and two different ones anticommute. Conjugating `τ_a` by another
member reverses its sign, so every member is traceless, and the trace pairs the members with
each other and with `1` orthonormally. Together with `1` they are linearly independent in the
four dimensional space of `2 × 2` matrices, so such a family has at most three members. The
Pauli matrices `σ1, σ2, σ3` attain the bound: they are a maximal anticommuting family, one for
each axis of space.

## ii. Key results

- `IsAnticommuting` : the relation `τ_a τ_b + τ_b τ_a = 2 δ_ab 1`.
- `IsAnticommuting.trace_mul`, `IsAnticommuting.trace_eq_zero` : the trace pairing.
- `IsAnticommuting.linearIndependent` : the members together with `1` are independent.
- `IsAnticommuting.card_le_three` : an anticommuting family has at most three members.
- `isAnticommuting_pauliMatrix` : the Pauli matrices are anticommuting.
- `isGreatest_card_isAnticommuting` : the largest anticommuting family has three members.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Anticommuting families
- B. At most three members
- C. The Pauli matrices attain the bound

## iv. References

* W. Pauli, *Zur Quantenmechanik des magnetischen Elektrons*, Z. Phys. 43 (1927) 601–623.

modules.title: The covariant Pauli matrices as plain matrices
modules.doc:
The Pauli matrices with the vector index lowered, and their completeness relation.

## i. Overview

`Physlib.Relativity.PauliMatrices.SelfAdjoint` carries the Pauli matrices as self-adjoint
matrices and as the basis `pauliBasis'` of the self-adjoint `2 × 2` matrices. Contracting
them against tensor components needs them as plain matrices, which is `pauliLower μ`, the
matrix underlying `pauliSelfAdjoint' μ`; `pauliBasis'_coe` identifies it with the basis vector
and `pauliLower_eq_smul` with `η_{μμ} σ^μ`. The Fierz completeness relation
`sum_pauliLower_mul_pauliLower` then says that these four matrices span the `2 × 2` matrices,
with the trace pairing as the duality and normalisation `2`; it is the relation which turns a
sum over a Lorentz index into a pair of Kronecker deltas on the spinor indices.

## ii. Key results

- `PauliMatrix.pauliLower` : the covariant Pauli matrices as plain matrices.
- `PauliMatrix.pauliBasis'_coe` : they underlie the basis `pauliBasis'`.
- `PauliMatrix.pauliLower_eq_smul` : lowering the index multiplies by the metric entry.
- `PauliMatrix.sum_pauliLower_mul_pauliLower` : the Fierz completeness relation.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The covariant Pauli matrices as plain matrices

## iv. References

The self-adjoint Pauli matrices and the basis `pauliBasis'` are in
`Physlib.Relativity.PauliMatrices.SelfAdjoint`.

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.pauliLower
declarations.doc:
The Pauli matrices with the vector index lowered by the Minkowski metric,
`σ_μ = η_{μμ} σ^μ`, as plain matrices: the underlying matrices of `pauliSelfAdjoint'`.
declarations.statement: def pauliLower (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ

declarations.doc: The covariant Pauli matrices are the underlying matrices of the basis `pauliBasis'`.
declarations.statement: lemma pauliBasis'_coe (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : (pauliBasis' μ).1 = pauliLower μ

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.pauliLower_eq_smul
declarations.doc: Lowering the vector index multiplies by the diagonal entry of the metric.
declarations.statement:
lemma pauliLower_eq_smul (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    pauliLower μ = ((minkowskiMatrixZ μ μ : ℤ) : ℂ) • pauliMatrix μ

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.sum_pauliLower_mul_pauliLower
declarations.doc:
The Fierz completeness relation: the covariant Pauli matrices span the `2 × 2` matrices,
with the trace pairing as the duality and normalisation `2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_pauliLower_mul_pauliLower (α α' β β' : Fin 2) :
    ∑ ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, pauliLower ρ β' β * pauliLower ρ α α'
      = 2 * ((if α = β then 1 else 0) * (if α' = β' then 1 else 0))

modules.title: The Pauli tensor in components
modules.doc:
The basis of `ℂT[.up, .upL, .upR]` indexed by a Lorentz and two spinor indices.

## i. Overview

`Physlib.Relativity.Bispinors.Pauli.ToTensor` carries the Pauli matrices as the tensor
`σ^^^ : ℂT[.up, .upL, .upR]` and the equivalence `indexEquiv` identifying the component index
of that tensor with a triple `(μ, α, β)`. Reindexing the tensor basis along `indexEquiv` gives
`indexBasis`, the basis labelled by such triples, and `toTensor_eq_sum_indexBasis` expands the
Pauli tensor in it: the coefficient of `e_μ ⊗ e_α ⊗ e_β` is the entry `σ^μ_{α β}`. This is the
form in which the Pauli tensor enters a component computation.

## ii. Key results

- `PauliMatrix.indexBasis` : the basis of `ℂT[.up, .upL, .upR]` indexed by `(μ, α, β)`.
- `PauliMatrix.toTensor_eq_sum_indexBasis` : `σ^^^ = ∑ σ^μ_{α β} e_μ ⊗ e_α ⊗ e_β`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The basis indexed by a Lorentz and two spinor indices

## iv. References

The Pauli tensor and `indexEquiv` are in `Physlib.Relativity.Bispinors.Pauli.ToTensor`.

modules.title: The Poincaré group
modules.doc:
The Poincaré group acts on spacetime by Lorentz transformations and translations.

## i. Overview

An element of the Poincaré group is a pair of a translation `a` and a Lorentz transformation `Λ`.
It acts on a point `x` by `x ↦ Λ x + a`. The group is built from the existing `LorentzGroup d`
and the vector group of `SpaceTime d`. The file also defines the action on functions of
spacetime by `(g • u) x = u (g⁻¹ x)`. A group element is orthochronous when its Lorentz part is.
The action on functions sends the support of a function to the image of the support.

## ii. Key results

- `PoincareGroup` : the group of translations and Lorentz transformations.
- `PoincareGroup.IsOrthochronous` : the Lorentz part preserves the direction of time.
- `PoincareGroup.act` : the action on functions of spacetime.
- `PoincareGroup.tsupport_act` : the support of `g • u` is the image of the support of `u`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The group
- B. The action on spacetime
- C. Orthochronous elements
- D. Point reflections
- E. The action on functions

## iv. References

None.

## A. The group

- `PoincareGroup` : the group of translations and Lorentz transformations.

## B. The action on spacetime

- `PoincareGroup.toHomeomorph` : each element is a homeomorphism of spacetime.

## C. Orthochronous elements

- `PoincareGroup.IsOrthochronous` : the Lorentz part preserves the direction of time.

## D. Point reflections

- `PoincareGroup.pointReflection` : the point reflection `x ↦ p - x`.
- `PoincareGroup.not_isOrthochronous_pointReflection` : it is not orthochronous.

## E. The action on functions

- `PoincareGroup.act` : the action `(g • u) x = u (g⁻¹ x)` on functions of spacetime.

modules.title: The causal structure is Poincaré invariant
modules.doc:
Orthochronous Poincaré transformations preserve causal futures and pasts.

## i. Overview

An event `q` causally follows `p` when the difference lies in the closed future light cone.
A Lorentz transformation preserves the Minkowski product. An orthochronous one also preserves the
direction of time, so it maps the future light cone to itself. A translation does not change
differences. So an orthochronous Poincaré transformation maps the causal future of a set to the
causal future of the image. A transformation that reverses time exchanges causal future and past.

## ii. Key results

- `causallyFollows_zero_smul` : orthochronous Lorentz maps preserve the future light cone.
- `causallyFollows_smul_iff` : orthochronous Poincaré maps preserve causal order.
- `causalFuture_smul` : the causal future of the image is the image of the causal future.
- `causalFuture_smul_of_not` : a time-reversing map sends the causal future to the causal past.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The future light cone
- B. The causal order
- C. Causal futures and pasts of sets

## iv. References

None.

## A. The future light cone

- `causallyFollows_zero_smul` : orthochronous Lorentz maps preserve the future light cone.

## B. The causal order

- `causallyFollows_smul_iff` : orthochronous Poincaré maps preserve causal order.

## C. Causal futures and pasts of sets

- `causalFuture_smul` : the causal future of the image is the image of the causal future.

modules.title: The Poincaré action on test functions and distributions
modules.doc:
The Poincaré group acts on test functions by pullback and on distributions by transposition.

## i. Overview

A Poincaré element `g` acts on a test function by `(g • φ) x = φ (g⁻¹ x)`. The action is
continuous on the space of test functions because pullback by a Lorentz transformation and by a
translation are. A distribution `T` is transformed by `(g • T) φ = T (g⁻¹ • φ)`. Then the
delta distribution at `p` goes to the delta distribution at `g p`. A distribution that vanishes
outside a set goes to a distribution that vanishes outside the image of the set.

## ii. Key results

- `PoincareGroup.actTestFunction` : the action on test functions.
- `PoincareGroup.actDist` : the action on distributions.
- `PoincareGroup.isVanishingOn_actDist` : the support of a transformed distribution.
- `PoincareGroup.actDist_delta` : the action sends a delta distribution to a delta distribution.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Test functions
- B. Distributions

## iv. References

None.

## A. Test functions

- `PoincareGroup.actTestFunction` : the action on test functions.

## B. Distributions

- `PoincareGroup.actDist` : the action on distributions.

modules.title: The Poincaré action on smooth fields

The Poincaré group acts on smooth fields and on compactly supported smooth fields.

## i. Overview

The action `(g • u) x = u (g⁻¹ x)` sends smooth functions to smooth functions. It is linear and

modules.title: The cyclic rotation and the half turns
modules.doc:
The rotation cycling the spatial axes, and the rotations by `π` about a coordinate axis.

## i. Overview

`Physlib.Relativity.SL2C.AxisRotations` carries the rotations taking the `z`-axis to a chosen
coordinate axis. Two further distinguished rotations are added here, both of which act on the
Lorentz index by a permutation or a sign and so can be used to relabel the axes in a
classification.

The cyclic rotation `rotationCycle` is the rotation by `2π/3` about the diagonal spatial axis.
Its Lorentz matrix is the permutation matrix of `cycDir`, the permutation fixing time and
sending `x → y → z → x`. Since `cycDir` has order three, an index family not fixed by it has
three distinct rotations, which is `cycDir_orbit_distinct`: that is what lets one axis of a
three-axis statement be proved and the other two obtained by relabelling.

The half turn `halfTurn k` is the rotation by `π` about the axis `k`, taken as the lift
`-i σ_k`. Its Lorentz matrix is diagonal: it fixes time and the axis and negates the two
transverse directions, with the signs recorded by `halfTurnSign`.

The spatial-axis convention is `0 = x`, `1 = y`, `2 = z`.

## ii. Key results

- `Lorentz.cycDir` : the cyclic permutation of Lorentz direction labels.
- `Lorentz.cycDir_cycDir_cycDir`, `Lorentz.cycDir_orbit_distinct` : it has order three, and an
  index family it does not fix has three distinct rotations.
- `Lorentz.SL2C.rotationCycle` : the cyclic rotation in `SL(2, ℂ)`.
- `Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup_rotationCycle_apply` : its Lorentz matrix is the permutation
  matrix of `cycDir`.
- `Lorentz.halfTurnSign`, `Lorentz.SL2C.halfTurn` : the half turn about a coordinate axis.
- `Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup_halfTurn_apply` : its diagonal Lorentz matrix.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The cyclic coordinate rotation
- B. Half turns about the coordinate axes

## iv. References

The rotations from the `z`-axis to a coordinate axis are in
`Physlib.Relativity.SL2C.AxisRotations`.

sections.text: ## A. The cyclic coordinate rotation

## B. Half turns about the coordinate axes

The half turn about the axis `k` is the rotation by `π` about it. It has two lifts to
`SL(2,ℂ)`, `-i σ_k` and `i σ_k`, which differ by the central element `-1` and have the same
Lorentz matrix. The chosen lift `halfTurn k` is `-i σ_k`, the value at `θ = π` of
`cos (θ / 2) - i sin (θ / 2) σ_k`, the convention `rotationCycle` also follows. Its Lorentz
matrix is diagonal: it fixes time and the axis and negates the two transverse directions, with
the signs recorded by `halfTurnSign`.

modules.title: Conjugation and the kernel of the covering map
modules.doc:
Entrywise conjugation on `SL(2, ℂ)`, and the covering map on `-1`, on entries and on adjoints.

## i. Overview

Three things about the covering map `SL(2, ℂ) →* LorentzGroup 3` are collected here, all
needed to carry a Lorentz index through a spinor computation.

Entrywise complex conjugation is a monoid endomorphism `conjHom` of `SL(2, ℂ)`, an involution,
and conjugating the group argument undoes the conjugation of the entries: the inverse
conjugate transpose at `conjHom g` is the inverse transpose at `g`. This is what lets a
right-handed slot be treated as a conjugated left-handed one.

The covering map sandwiches, `A ↦ M A Mᴴ`, so the two signs of `-1` cancel and
`toLorentzGroup (-1) = 1`: the map is two-to-one. It also intertwines conjugate transposition
with matrix transposition, `L(M†) = L(M)ᵀ`.

Finally `sum_pauliLower_mul_sl2c` is the defining intertwining identity read entrywise:
sandwiching `σ_μ` between `g` and `gᴴ` mixes the covariant Pauli matrices by the column `μ` of
the Lorentz matrix of `g`.

## ii. Key results

- `Lorentz.SL2C.conjHom` : entrywise conjugation as a monoid endomorphism.
- `Lorentz.SL2C.conjHom_involutive`, `Lorentz.SL2C.conjHom_inv_conjTranspose` : its
  involutivity, and its effect on the inverse conjugate transpose.
- `Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup_neg_one` : the centre covers the identity.
- `Lorentz.SL2C.sum_pauliLower_mul_sl2c` : the intertwining identity on entries.
- `Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup_conjTranspose` : `L(M†) = L(M)ᵀ`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Entrywise conjugation
- B. The kernel of the covering map
- C. The intertwining identity on entries
- D. The covering map and adjoints

## iv. References

The covering map and its properties are in `Physlib.Relativity.SL2C.Basic`.

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.conjHom
declarations.doc:
Entrywise complex conjugation as a monoid endomorphism of `SL(2,ℂ)`: Mathlib's
`SpecialLinearGroup.map` along `starRingEnd ℂ`.
declarations.statement: abbrev conjHom : SL(2,ℂ) →* SL(2,ℂ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.conjHom_coe
declarations.statement: lemma conjHom_coe (g : SL(2,ℂ)) : (conjHom g).1 = g.1.map star

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.conjHom_involutive
declarations.doc: Conjugation is an involution, hence surjective.
declarations.statement: lemma conjHom_involutive : Function.Involutive conjHom

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.conjHom_inv_conjTranspose
declarations.doc:
Conjugating the group argument undoes the conjugation of the entries: the inverse
conjugate transpose at `conjHom g` is the inverse transpose at `g`.
declarations.statement: lemma conjHom_inv_conjTranspose (g : SL(2,ℂ)) : (((conjHom g).1)⁻¹)ᴴ = (g.1⁻¹)ᵀ

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup_neg_one
declarations.doc:
**The centre of `SL(2, ℂ)` covers the identity Lorentz transformation.** The covering
map sandwiches, `A ↦ M A Mᴴ`, so the two signs of `-1` cancel. Together with
`_root_.map_one` this says that the covering map is two-to-one.
declarations.statement: lemma toLorentzGroup_neg_one : toLorentzGroup (-1) = 1

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.sum_pauliLower_mul_sl2c
declarations.doc:
The intertwining identity `toSelfAdjointMap_basis` read entrywise: sandwiching the
covariant Pauli matrix `σ_μ` between `g` and `gᴴ` mixes the covariant Pauli matrices by the
column `μ` of the Lorentz matrix of `g`, the summed Lorentz index first.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_pauliLower_mul_sl2c (g : SL(2,ℂ)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (β β' : Fin 2) :
    ∑ p : Fin 2 × Fin 2, PauliMatrix.pauliLower μ p.1 p.2 * (g.1 β p.1 * star (g.1 β' p.2))
      = ∑ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, (((toLorentzGroup g).1 ν μ : ℝ) : ℂ)
        * PauliMatrix.pauliLower ν β β'

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup_conjTranspose
declarations.doc:
The covering map intertwines conjugate transposition with matrix
transposition: `L(M†) = L(M)ᵀ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma toLorentzGroup_conjTranspose {M N : SL(2,ℂ)} (hN : N.1 = M.1ᴴ) :
    (toLorentzGroup N).1 = (toLorentzGroup M).1ᵀ

modules.title: The dual of the complex covector representation
modules.doc:
How dual complex covectors transform, on the dual basis.

## i. Overview

A covector representation induces one on the dual space, and a classification of invariant
tensors has to know how the dual basis transforms. For the complex covectors
`Lorentz.ComplexCoVector` the answer is that dual covectors transform contravariantly: the dual
basis vector `e^μ` goes to the combination of dual basis vectors given by the column `μ` of the
complexified Lorentz matrix. This is the complex analogue of
`Lorentz.CoVector.sl2Rep_dual_dualBasis`, and is obtained from
`Representation.dual_apply_dualBasis` with the transposed inverse matrix read off from
`Lorentz.ComplexCoVector.basis_ρ_apply`.

## ii. Key results

- `Lorentz.ComplexCoVector.SL2CRep_dual_dualBasis` : dual complex covectors transform by the columns
  of the complexified Lorentz matrix.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The dual representation on the dual basis

## iv. References

The complex covector representation is in
`Physlib.Relativity.Tensors.ComplexTensor.Vector.Basic`.
